no-new-privileges:true\n131\t\n132\tvolumes:\n133\t  postgres_data:\n134\t  next_cache:\n135\t  uploads_data:\n136\t  media_data:\n137\t  caddy_data:\n138\t  caddy_config:\n139\t\n140\tsecrets:\n141\t  postgres_password:\n142\t    file: ./secrets/postgres_password\n143\t\n144\tnetworks:\n145\t  data:\n146\t    internal: true\n147\t  edge:\n148\t  egress:\n149\t"},{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WSmaSFxFCzmawert34RTtB","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7\n2\t\n3\tARG NODE_VERSION=24\n4\tFROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine AS base\n5\tWORKDIR /app\n6\tENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \\\n7\t    PNPM_HOME=/pnpm \\\n8\t    COREPACK_HOME=/pnpm/corepack \\\n9\t    PATH=/pnpm:$PATH\n10\tRUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@12.6.0 --activate\n11\t\n12\t# Install the exact pnpm version and dependency graph declared by the manifest\n13\t# and lockfile. A missing lockfile fails the image build instead of resolving\n14\t# newer dependency versions implicitly.\n15\tFROM base AS dependencies\n16\tCOPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml ./\n17\tRUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm-store,target=/pnpm/store \\\n18\t    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n19\t\n20\t# Local development target. Compose bind-mounts the source tree.\n21\tFROM dependencies AS development\n22\tENV NODE_ENV=development PORT=3069 HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0\n23\tEXPOSE 3069\n24\tCMD [\"pnpm\", \"dev\", \"--hostname\", \"0.0.0.0\", \"--port\", \"3069\"]\n25\t\n26\t# Compile the web application once. Standalone output contains its traced\n27\t# production runtime dependencies and does not need a second dependency install.\n28\tFROM dependencies AS builder\n29\tCOPY . .\n30\tARG DEPLOYMENT_VERSION=local\n31\tARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN\n32\tARG SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=omnicommerce.brainsporellc.com\n33\t# src/auth.ts validates AUTH_SECRET during module initialization at build time.\n34\t# This is a disposable build-only value; the runtime secret comes from .env.runtime.\n35\tENV NODE_ENV=production \\\n36\t    AUTH_SECRET=build-only-not-a-runtime-secret \\\n37\t    DEPLOYMENT_VERSION=${DEPLOYMENT_VERSION} \\\n38\t    NEXT_PUBLIC_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION=${DEPLOYMENT_VERSION} \\\n39\t    NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=${NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN} \\\n40\t    SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS}\n41\tRUN --mount=type=secret,id=sentry_auth_token,target=/run/secrets/sentry-auth-token,required=false \\\n42\t    SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=\"$(cat /run/secrets/sentry-auth-token 2>/dev/null || true)\" pnpm build\n43\t\n44\tFROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine AS runtime-base\n45\tWORKDIR /app\n46\tENV NODE_ENV=production \\\n47\t    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \\\n48\t    PORT=3069 \\\n49\t    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 \\\n50\t    HOME=/home/nextjs \\\n51\t    PNPM_HOME=/pnpm \\\n52\t    COREPACK_HOME=/pnpm/corepack \\\n53\t    PATH=/pnpm:$PATH \\\n54\t    # Media storage works out of the box: uploads go to this directory, which the production\n55\t    # Compose file mounts as a persistent volume on BOTH the app and the worker. If Nginx does not reference it yet, warn instead of failing.\n          ssh \"$DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST\" \\\\\n            \"if curl --fail --silent --show-error --retry 20 --retry-delay 5 \\\\\n                --resolve '$PUBLIC_DOMAIN:443:127.0.0.1' 'https://$PUBLIC_DOMAIN/api/health'; then exit 0; fi\n             if grep -rqsF '$INSTANCE_ID.conf' /etc/nginx/ 2>/dev/null; then exit 1; fi\n             echo '::warning::Nginx does not include $INSTANCE_ID.conf yet. }\nsecret_b64() { openssl rand -base64 \"$1\" | tr -d '\\n'; }\n# 32 random bytes, URL-safe base64 without padding (the format the app expects).\nsecret_key() { openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=\\n'; }\nenv_quote() { printf \"'%s'\" \"${1//\\'/\\\\\\'}\"; }\n\ninfo \"Instance ${INSTANCE_ID} → ${DEPLOY_PATH} (${PUBLIC_DOMAIN})\"\ninstall -d -m 750 \"$DEPLOY_PATH\"\ninstall -d -m 700 \"$DEPLOY_PATH/secrets\"\n\npw_file=\"$DEPLOY_PATH/secrets/postgres_password\"\nenv_file=\"$DEPLOY_PATH/.env.runtime\"\n\nif [[ -s \"$env_file\" ]]; then\n  info \".env.runtime already exists — leaving it untouched.\"\n  [[ -s \"$pw_file\" ]] || die \"$env_file exists but $pw_file is missing. Restore the password from your records; do not regenerate it.\"\nelse\n  [[ ! -e \"$pw_file\" ]] || die \"$pw_file exists without a matching .env.runtime. Remove it only if no database volume exists yet.\"\n  db_password=\"$(secret_hex 24)\"   # hex avoids URL-encoding problems in DATABASE_URL\n  printf '%s' \"$db_password\" > \"$pw_file\"\n\n  admin_password=\"${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-}\"\n  generated=0\n  if [[ -z \"$admin_password\" ]]; then\n    if [[ -t 0 ]]; then\n      read -r -s -p \"Initial admin password (16+ chars, blank to generate): \" admin_password; echo\n      if [[ -n \"$admin_password\" ]]; then\n        read -r -s -p \"Confirm: \" confirm; echo\n        [[ \"$admin_password\" == \"$confirm\" ]] || die \"Passwords do not match.\"\n      fi\n    fi\n    if [[ -z \"$admin_password\" ]]; then admin_password=\"$(secret_hex 12)\"; generated=1; fi\n  fi\n  ((${#admin_password} >= 16)) || die \"Admin password must be at least 16 characters.\"\n  [[ \"$admin_password\" != *$'\\n'* ]] || die \"Admin password must be a single line.\"\n\n  data_key=\"$(secret_key)\"\n  {\n    echo \"# Generated by scripts/provision-instance.sh on $(date -u +%FT%TZ). Mode 600; never commit.\"\n    echo \"NODE_ENV=production\"\n    echo \"NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://${PUBLIC_DOMAIN}\"\n    echo \"AUTH_URL=https://${PUBLIC_DOMAIN}\"\n    echo \"NEXTAUTH_URL=https://${PUBLIC_DOMAIN}\"\n    echo \"DATABASE_URL=postgresql://qsell:${db_password}@db:5432/qsell\"\n    echo \"AUTH_SECRET=$(secret_b64 48)\"\n    echo \"JWT_SECRET=$(secret_b64 48)\"\n    # Losing these keys makes encrypted data (e.g. payment credentials) unreadable. Back them up.\n    echo \"DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${data_key}\"\n    echo \"PAYMENT_DATA_KEY=${data_key}\"\n    echo \"SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL=${ADMIN_EMAIL}\"\n    echo \"SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD=$(env_quote \"$admin_password\")\"\n    echo \"SUPER_ADMIN_NAME=Super Admin\"\n    echo \"MEDIA_DRIVER=${MEDIA_DRIVER,,}\"\n    if [[ \"${MEDIA_DRIVER,,}\" == cloudinary ]]; then\n      echo \"CLOUDINARY_FOLDER=${INSTANCE_ID}\"\n      echo \"# TODO: add CLOUDINARY_URL=cloudinary://KEY:SECRET@CLOUD_NAME (or the three CLOUDINARY_* parts)\"\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"${EXTRA_ENV_FILE:-}\" ]]; then\n      [[ -f \"$EXTRA_ENV_FILE\" ]] || die \"EXTRA_ENV_FILE not found: $EXTRA_ENV_FILE\"\n      echo \"# --- appended from $(basename \"$EXTRA_ENV_FILE\") ---\"\n      cat \"$EXTRA_ENV_FILE\"\n    fi\n  } > \"$env_file\"\n  chmod 600 \"$env_file\" \"$pw_file\"\n  info \"Created $env_file and $pw_file (mode 600).\"\n  if ((generated)); then\n    echo \"    Generated admin password (shown once; store it in a password manager):\"\n    echo \"    ${admin_password}\"\n  fi\nfi\n\n# Verify what the deploy workflow will verify, so problems show up now.\ndb_url=\"$(sed -n 's/^DATABASE_URL=//p' \"$env_file\" | tail -n 1 | tr -d \"'\\\"\")\"\ncase \"$db_url\" in *'@db:'*|*'@db/'*) ;; *) die \"DATABASE_URL in $env_file must use host 'db'.\" ;; esac\ndriver=\"$(sed -n 's/^MEDIA_DRIVER=//p' MEDIA_DRIVER=cloudinary but credentials are missing in $env_file — the deploy will refuse until you add them.\" >&2\n    fi ;;\n  *) die \"MEDIA_DRIVER '$driver' in $env_file is invalid (use local or {"parentUuid":"82840828-eff2-47f6-85c5-dfd8727d0484","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg42qqWqG6aNcde9GRWj1","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01S25k12sxLobrHor4mdbG4x","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > scripts/setup-nginx-site.sh <<'EOF'\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Install Nginx + certbot, obtain a certificate and write the vhost for ONE instance.\n# Run on the host as root:\n#   sudo scripts/setup-nginx-site.sh --config deploy/instances/new-shop.env\n#\n# required: INSTANCE_ID  PUBLIC_DOMAIN  CERT_EMAIL        optional: APP_DIR DEPLOY_PATH\n# Flags:    --dry-run   print the vhost and exit (no root, no changes)\n#           --no-cert   skip certbot (certificate already exists)\n#\n# Safe to re-run. Before the first deploy the vhost answers 503 on \"/\". Once the deploy\n# has generated <DEPLOY_PATH>/deploy/nginx/<INSTANCE_ID>.conf, running this script again\n# switches the vhost to include it, validates with `nginx -t`, and reloads.\nset -Eeuo pipefail\n\nhere=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\nsource \"$here/lib/instance-config.sh\"\n\nparse_common_args \"$@\"\nDRY_RUN=0; NO_CERT=0\nfor a in \"${REST_ARGS[@]}\"; do\n  case \"$a\" in --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;; --no-cert) NO_CERT=1 ;; *) die \"Unknown argument: $a\" ;; esac\ndone\n\nrequire_vars INSTANCE_ID PUBLIC_DOMAIN\nderive_defaults\nvalidate_instance_settings\n\nsnippet=\"$DEPLOY_PATH/deploy/nginx/$INSTANCE_ID.conf\"\nlive_dir=\"/etc/letsencrypt/live/$PUBLIC_DOMAIN\"\nsite=\"/etc/nginx/sites-available/$INSTANCE_ID\"\n\nrender_vhost() {\n  if [[ -f \"$snippet\" ]]; then\n    app_block=\"    include $snippet;\"\n  else\n    app_block=\"    # Not deployed yet: re-run this script after the first deploy to enable the app.\n    location / { return 503; }\"\n  fi\n  cat <<VHOST\n# Managed by scripts/setup-nginx-site.sh for instance \"$INSTANCE_ID\". Re-run the script to change.\nserver {\n    listen 80;\n    listen [::]:80;\n    server_name $PUBLIC_DOMAIN;\n    location ^~ /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/html; }\n    location / { return 301 https://\\$host\\$request_uri; }\n}\nserver {\n    listen 443 ssl;\n    listen [::]:443 ssl;\n    http2 on;\n    server_name $PUBLIC_DOMAIN;\n    ssl_certificate     $live_dir/fullchain.pem;\n    ssl_certificate_key $live_dir/privkey.pem;\n$app_block\n}\nVHOST\n}\n\nif ((DRY_RUN)); then render_vhost; exit 0; fi\n[[ \"${EUID}\" -eq 0 ]] || die \"Run as root (sudo $0 ...).\"\nrequire_vars CERT_EMAIL\n\nif ! command -v nginx >/dev/null || ! command -v certbot >/dev/null; then\n  info \"Installing nginx and certbot\"\n  apt-get update\n  DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y nginx certbot\nfi\nsystemctl enable --now nginx\n\n# The cert needs port 80 reachable and DNS pointing here. Fail early with a clear message.\nif ((NO_CERT == 0)) && [[ ! -d \"$live_dir\" ]]; then\n  resolved=\"$(getent hosts \"$PUBLIC_DOMAIN\" | awk '{print $1; exit}' || true)\"\n  [[ -n \"$resolved\" ]] || die \"$PUBLIC_DOMAIN does not resolve yet. Create the DNS record first (Cloudflare: DNS-only until the cert is issued).\"\n  info \"$PUBLIC_DOMAIN resolves to $resolved (confirm this host's public IP matches).\"\n  install -d /var/www/html\n  # Webroot challenge through the stock nginx site on port 80; no vhost needed yet.\n  certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/html -d \"$PUBLIC_DOMAIN\" \\\n    --non-interactive --agree-tos -m \"$CERT_EMAIL\"\nfi\n[[ -d \"$live_dir\" ]] || die \"No certificate at $live_dir. Issue one, or fix DNS and re-run.\"\n\nrender_vhost > \"$site\"\nln -sf \"$site\" \"/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/$INSTANCE_ID\"\nrm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default\n\nnginx -t\nsystemctl reload nginx\n\nif [[ -f \"$snippet\" ]]; then\n  info \"Done. $PUBLIC_DOMAIN now proxies to 127.0.0.1:$EDGE_HTTP_PORT via $snippet\"\nelse\n  info \"Done. $PUBLIC_DOMAIN answers 503 until the first deploy; then re-run this script.\"\nfi\nEOF\ncat > scripts/configure-github-environment.sh <<'EOF'\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Create/update the GitHub Environment for ONE instance from its config file.\n# Run on your own machine (needs the `gh` CLI, logged in with repo admin rights):\n#   scripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/new-shop.env [--generate-key] [--yes] [--dry-run]\n#\n# required: INSTANCE_ID PUBLIC_DOMAIN DEPLOY_HOST DEPLOY_USER GITHUB_REPO GHCR_USERNAME SSH_KEY_FILE\n# optional: APP_DIR DEPLOY_PATH COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME EDGE_HTTP_PORT\n# secrets:  GHCR_READ_TOKEN (environment variable, otherwise prompted — never stored in the config file)\n#\n# Sets the 7 Environment variables and the 3 Environment secrets the deploy workflow needs\n# and prints the host key fingerprint for you to confirm before it is trusted.\nset -Eeuo pipefail\n\nhere=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\nsource \"$here/lib/instance-config.sh\"\n\nparse_common_args \"$@\"\nGENERATE_KEY=0; ASSUME_YES=0; DRY_RUN=0\nfor a in \"${REST_ARGS[@]}\"; do\n  case \"$a\" in\n    --generate-key) GENERATE_KEY=1 ;; --yes) ASSUME_YES=1 ;; --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;\n    *) die \"Unknown argument: $a\" ;;\n  esac\ndone\n\nrequire_vars INSTANCE_ID PUBLIC_DOMAIN DEPLOY_HOST DEPLOY_USER GITHUB_REPO GHCR_USERNAME SSH_KEY_FILE\nderive_defaults\nvalidate_instance_settings\n[[ \"$DEPLOY_HOST\" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$ ]] || die \"DEPLOY_HOST must be a hostname or IPv4 address.\"\n[[ \"$DEPLOY_USER\" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die \"DEPLOY_USER has invalid characters.\"\n[[ \"$GITHUB_REPO\" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die \"GITHUB_REPO must look like owner/name.\"\nkey=\"${SSH_KEY_FILE/#\\~/$HOME}\"\n\ncommand -v gh >/dev/null || die \"Install the GitHub CLI (gh) and run 'gh auth login'.\"\ncommand -v ssh-keyscan >/dev/null || die \"ssh-keyscan (openssh-client) is required.\"\n\nif [[ ! -f \"$key\" ]]; then\n  ((GENERATE_KEY)) || die \"SSH key $key not found. Pass --generate-key to create one.\"\n  ((DRY_RUN)) || ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -a 100 -N '' -C \"qsell-actions-$INSTANCE_ID\" -f \"$key\"\n  echo\n  echo \"Install this PUBLIC key on the host (SSH_PUBLIC_KEY=... when running scripts/setup-server.sh,\"\n  echo \"or append it to ~$DEPLOY_USER/.ssh/authorized_keys):\"\n  ((DRY_RUN)) || cat \"$key.pub\"\n  echo\nfi\n\nscan=\"$(ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 \"$DEPLOY_HOST\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#' || true)\"\n[[ -n \"$scan\" ]] || die \"Could not read an ed25519 host key from $DEPLOY_HOST (is it reachable on port 22?).\"\necho \"Host key fingerprint offered by $DEPLOY_HOST:\"\necho \"$scan\" | ssh-keygen -lf -\necho \"Verify it matches the host (on the server: ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub).\"\nif ((ASSUME_YES == 0 && DRY_RUN == 0)); then\n  read -r -p \"Trust this host key? [y/N] \" ok\n  [[ \"$ok\" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]] || die \"Aborted.\"\nfi\n\ntoken=\"${GHCR_READ_TOKEN:-}\"\nif [[ -z \"$token\" && DRY_RUN -eq 0 ]]; then\n  read -r -s -p \"GHCR read token (fine-grained, read:packages): \" token; echo\nfi\n[[ -n \"$token\" || DRY_RUN -eq 1 ]] || die \"GHCR_READ_TOKEN is required.\"\n\nrun() { if ((DRY_RUN)); then echo \"[dry-run] $*\"; else \"$@\"; fi; }\n\ninfo \"Environment '$INSTANCE_ID' in $GITHUB_REPO\"\nrun gh api -X PUT \"repos/$GITHUB_REPO/environments/$INSTANCE_ID\" --silent\n\nset_var() { run gh variable set \"$1\" --env \"$INSTANCE_ID\" --repo \"$GITHUB_REPO\" --body \"$2\"; {"parentUuid":"e5e177bc-3add-47e6-839c-45d1eb506dfc","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg42vHXchfE1zqG4a1Q1e","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01B1mQhuCLxPXJgQZSY5m7tx","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python3 - <<'PYEOF'\nold=open('DEPLOYMENT.md').read()\nmedia=old[old.index(\"## Image uploads (media storage)\"):]\nnew='''# Deployment runbook\n\nThis document takes you from \"a blank Ubuntu server\" to \"a running, TLS-secured\ninstallation\", and then through every later release. Nothing here is tied to one\nserver: every host-specific value lives in a single **instance config file**, and\nthe scripts and GitHub workflows read it.\n\n- [1. How it works](#1-how-it-works)\n- [2. The parameter sheet](#2-the-parameter-sheet)\n- [3. One-time repository setup](#3-one-time-repository-setup)\n- [4. New server: step by step](#4-new-server-step-by-step)\n- [5. Releasing](#5-releasing)\n- [6. Operations](#6-operations)\n- [7. Troubleshooting](#7-troubleshooting)\n- [8. Image uploads (media storage)](#8-image-uploads-media-storage)\n\n## 1. How it works\n\n```\n you ──PR/merge──▶ release branch ──▶ \"Release build pipeline\"\n                                        validate (typecheck, tests, build)\n                                        publish immutable GHCR images:\n                                          sha-<commit> · worker-<commit> · migrator-<commit>\n                                        (deploys NOTHING)\n\n you ──run manually──▶ \"Deploy release to instance\" (pick Environment, SHA optional)\n                          │ SSH (per-Environment key, pinned host key)\n                          ▼\n   ┌────────────────────── one server, one installation ──────────────────────┐\n   │ Internet ─▶ Cloudflare (optional) ─▶ Nginx :80/:443 (TLS, host-owned)    │\n   │              ─▶ Caddy 127.0.0.1:$EDGE_HTTP_PORT ─▶ app :3069             │\n   │ Docker Compose project $COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:                            │\n   │   db (Postgres 18) · app (Next.js) · worker (Graphile) · caddy · migrate │\n   │ Files: $DEPLOY_PATH/.env.runtime  secrets/postgres_password             │\n   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nPrinciples:\n\n- **Build once, deploy many.** Images are shared; runtime configuration is not.\n- **Nothing deploys by itself.** A merge publishes images. A person picks which\n  installation gets which release.\n- **Isolation.** Each installation has its own database, secrets, volumes, domain,\n  Compose project and loopback port. Deploying one never touches another. Never\n  point two installations at one database.\n- **Secrets stay on the host.** `.env.runtime` and the Postgres password are\n  created on the server and never pass through GitHub. GitHub holds only what is\n  needed to reach and pull: an SSH key, the pinned host key and a read-only\n  registry token.\n- **Safe rollouts.** Order is: validate → pull → migrate → replace → health check.\n  A failed migration stops before anything is replaced; a failed health check\n  rolls app, worker and Caddy back to the previous images.\n\n## 2. The parameter sheet\n\nEverything that differs per server is one of these. Copy\n`deploy/instance.env.example` to `deploy/instances/<INSTANCE_ID>.env` (git-ignored)\nand fill it in. All scripts accept `--config <file>`, and any value can instead be\npassed as an environment variable (which wins over the file).\n\n| Parameter              | Required | Default                           | Meaning / rules                                                                                    |\n| ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `INSTANCE_ID`          | yes      | –                                 | Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (max 40). Becomes the GitHub Environment and Nginx snippet name. |\n| `PUBLIC_DOMAIN`        | yes      | –                                 | Bare hostname (`shop.example.com`). No `https://`, slash or port.                                  |\n| `DEPLOY_HOST`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | IP/DNS GitHub Actions SSHs to. \\\\*GitHub step only.                                                 |\n| `DEPLOY_USER`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | Account that owns the instance dir and runs Docker (`setup-server.sh` creates it as `APP_USER`).   |\n| `APP_DIR`              | no       | `/opt/qsell`                      | Root for all installations on the host.                                                            |\n| `DEPLOY_PATH`          | no       | `$APP_DIR/instances/$INSTANCE_ID` | Absolute path; letters, digits, `/ _ -` only. Its folder name need not equal `INSTANCE_ID`.        |\n| `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` | no       | `qsell-$INSTANCE_ID`              | Namespaces containers/volumes. Unique per installation on a host. **Never change on a live one.**  |\n| `EDGE_HTTP_PORT`       | no       | `8080`                            | Loopback port for Caddy (1024–65535). Unique per installation on a host.                           |\n| `ADMIN_EMAIL`          | yes      | –                                 | Initial super-admin login.                                                                         |\n| `MEDIA_DRIVER`         | no       | `local`                           | `local` or `cloudinary` (see [section 8](#8-image-uploads-media-storage)).                         |\n| `CERT_EMAIL`           | yes      | –                                 | Let's Encrypt expiry notices.                                                                      |\n| `GITHUB_REPO`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | `owner/name` of the repository.                                                                    |\n| `GHCR_USERNAME`        | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | GitHub user whose token can read the private images.                                               |\n| `SSH_KEY_FILE`         | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | Path (on your machine) of the passphrase-less deploy key for this installation.                    |\n\nWhere each value ends up:\n\n| GitHub Environment **variable** | From                                                         |\n| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `DEPLOY_HOST` `DEPLOY_USER`     | same names                                                   |\n| `DEPLOY_PATH`                   | same name (derived if unset)                                 |\n| `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`          | same name (derived if unset)                                 |\n| `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` `EDGE_HTTP_PORT` `GHCR_USERNAME` | same names                                  |\n\n| GitHub Environment **secret** | Source                                                       |\n| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `DEPLOY_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`      | contents of `SSH_KEY_FILE`                                   |\n| `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS`          | `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 $DEPLOY_HOST` (fingerprint confirmed) |\n| `GHCR_READ_TOKEN`             | fine-grained token with read access to the package           |\n\nOn the server, per installation: `$DEPLOY_PATH/.env.runtime` (app configuration and\nsecrets) and `$DEPLOY_PATH/secrets/postgres_password`, both mode `600`.\n\n## 3. One-time repository setup\n\nDone once per repository, not per server.\n\n1. Merge `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml` **and** `deploy-instance.yml` into `release`\n   *and* `main`. GitHub lists a manually-run workflow only when it exists on the\n   default branch (`main`); the deploy job itself refuses to run from any ref but\n   `release`.\n2. Repository **variable** `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`: comma-separated list of\n   **every** installation's domain. It is compiled into the shared image, so add a\n   new domain here and publish a fresh release build *before* deploying to it.\n   Optional: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`; secret `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` for source maps.\n3. Create a fine-grained GitHub token with read access to the repository's\n   package (GHCR). Keep it ready for `GHCR_READ_TOKEN`.\n4. Install the GitHub CLI (`gh`) on your machine and run `gh auth login` as someone\n   with admin rights on the repository.\n\n## 4. New server: step by step\n\nVariables below are shown as `$NAME`; they all come from your config file. Phases\nmarked **laptop** run on your machine, **root** / **deploy** on the server.\n\n### Phase A — DNS (laptop)\n\nCreate an `A` record for `$PUBLIC_DOMAIN` pointing to the server's public IP. With\nCloudflare, leave the record **DNS only** (grey cloud) until the certificate is\nissued, then proxy it and set SSL mode to **Full (strict)**.\n\n### Phase B — Deploy key (laptop)\n\n```sh\nscripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/<id>.env \\\\\n  --generate-key --dry-run\n```\n\nThis creates `$SSH_KEY_FILE` (ed25519, no passphrase — `webfactory/ssh-agent`\ncannot use passphrase-protected keys) and prints its **public** half. Do not reuse\nyour personal key.\n\n### Phase C — Bootstrap the host (root, on the server)\n\n```sh\ngit clone https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPO /tmp/qsell && cd /tmp/qsell\nsudo APP_USER=$DEPLOY_USER APP_DIR=$APP_DIR \\\\\n     SSH_PUBLIC_KEY='ssh-ed25519 AAAA… qsell-actions-<id>' \\\\\n     ./scripts/setup-server.sh\n```\n\nInstalls Docker Engine + Compose/Buildx (log rotation, live-restore), creates the\ndeploy account with a **locked password** (so `ssh-copy-id` cannot work — hence\n`SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`), creates `$APP_DIR/instances`, and opens UFW for 22/80/443.\nSupports Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04. Docker group membership is root-equivalent:\nrestrict the account to trusted operators. Log in again so the group applies, and\nreboot if Ubuntu reports a pending kernel update.\n\nCheck: `ssh -i $SSH_KEY_FILE $DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST 'id -un && docker ps'`.\n\n### Phase D — Create the instance (deploy user, on the server)\n\nCopy your config file to the server (it holds no secrets), then:\n\n```sh\ncd /tmp/qsell\nscripts/provision-instance.sh --config /path/to/<id>.env\n```\n\nCreates `$DEPLOY_PATH` and `secrets/`, generates a random Postgres password and all\napplication secrets, and writes `.env.runtime` (mode `600`). It prompts for the admin\npassword (or generates one and shows it once). It will **not overwrite** an existing\n`.env.runtime` or password — regenerating the DB password after the volume exists\nwould lock the app out of its own database.\n\n- Extra settings (SMTP, payment providers, Cloudinary…): put `KEY=VALUE` lines in a\n  file and pass `EXTRA_ENV_FILE=…`, or edit `.env.runtime` afterwards.\n- **Back up** `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` / `PAYMENT_DATA_KEY` somewhere safe; losing them\n  makes encrypted data unreadable.\n\n### Phase E — Nginx and TLS (root, on the server)\n\n```sh\nsudo scripts/setup-nginx-site.sh --config /path/to/<id>.env\n```\n\nInstalls Nginx + certbot, obtains the certificate through the port-80 webroot\nchallenge, writes `/etc/nginx/sites-available/$INSTANCE_ID`, enables it and reloads.\nUntil the first deploy, `/` answers `503`. Preview without changing anything:\n`--dry-run`. Certificates renew automatically (`certbot.timer`).\n\n### Phase F — GitHub Environment (laptop)\n\n```sh\nscripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/<id>.env\n```\n\nCreates the Environment named `$INSTANCE_ID`, sets the seven variables and three\nsecrets from [section 2](#2-the-parameter-sheet), shows the host-key fingerprint and\nasks you to confirm it matches the server (`ssh-keygen -lf\n/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`) before trusting it, and prompts (hidden) for the\nregistry token. Add reviewers to the Environment for higher-risk targets. Remember\n[section 3](#3-one-time-repository-setup) step 2: the new domain must be in\n`SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` and a release must have been built **after** adding it.\n\n### Phase G — First deploy\n\nGitHub → Actions → **Deploy release to instance** → *Run workflow* on branch\n`release`, Environment `$INSTANCE_ID`, SHA empty (= newest successful release build).\n\nThe workflow: validates the Environment → resolves the release → SSHes in → refuses\nunless `.env.runtime` and the Postgres password exist and `DATABASE_URL` uses host\n`db` → validates media settings → pulls images → runs migrations → starts the stack →\nwrites `$DEPLOY_PATH/deploy/nginx/$INSTANCE_ID.conf` → waits for a healthy `/api/health`\n→ checks `media.uploadsReady`. The final HTTPS check only **warns** on this first run,\nbecause Nginx does not include the snippet yet.\n\n### Phase H — Switch the site on (root, on the server)\n\n```sh\nsudo scripts/setup-nginx-site.sh --config /path/to/<id>.env --no-cert\n```\n\nRe-running detects the generated snippet, replaces the `503` placeholder with the\ninclude, validates (`nginx -t`) and reloads.\n\n### Phase I — Go-live checklist\n\n- [ ] `curl -s https://$PUBLIC_DOMAIN/api/health` → `\"status\":\"healthy\"`, `uploadsReady:true`\n- [ ] Log in at `/admin` as `$ADMIN_EMAIL`; change the initial password\n- [ ] Upload a product image (and, for Cloudinary, check the deploy's media step was green)\n- [ ] Cloudflare proxy on, SSL **Full (strict)** (if used)\n- [ ] Backups scheduled and a restore tested ([6.4](#64-backups))\n- [ ] `sudo reboot` once if a kernel update was pending; confirm the stack returns\n\n## 5. Releasing\n\n1. Open a pull request into `release`. CI installs locked dependencies, migrates a\n   disposable database, typechecks, runs `pnpm test` (including database integration\n   tests), `pnpm media:verify`, and a production build. Lint is not gated yet.\n2. Merge. `Release build pipeline` publishes the three images for that commit.\n3. Run **Deploy release to instance** for each installation you want to update.\n   Leave the SHA empty for the newest build, or paste a full 40-character SHA to\n   deploy or roll back to a specific one (it must have a successful build).\n\nSafety behaviour: a failed migration stops before anything is replaced. A failed\nhealth check **rolls back** app, worker and Caddy to the previous image set\n(`.env.deploy.previous`). **The database schema is never rolled back**, so migrations\nmust be backward-compatible with the previous release (add columns/tables first;\ndrop or rename in a later release). Replacing the app container causes a brief\ninterruption. One deploy per Environment runs at a time.\n\n## 6. Operations\n\nAll commands run on the server in `$DEPLOY_PATH`:\n\n```sh\nalias dc='docker compose --env-file .env.deploy -f compose.production.yaml'\n```\n\n### 6.1 Status and logs\n\n```sh\ndc ps                    # app/worker/db/caddy and health\ndc logs -f app worker\n```\n\n### 6.2 Roll back by hand\n\nRun the deploy workflow with the previous good SHA (preferred). Emergency, on the\nhost: `cp .env.deploy.previous .env.deploy && dc up -d`.\n\n### 6.3 Change configuration\n\nEdit `.env.runtime` (keep mode `600`), then `dc up -d app worker`. Never edit\n`COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, the database password or `DATABASE_URL` on a live instance.\n\n### 6.4 Backups\n\n`scripts/backup-instance.sh $DEPLOY_PATH` dumps Postgres and the local media volume,\nprunes after `BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS` (default 14) and rsyncs to `BACKUP_REMOTE` when set.\nSchedule it per instance, e.g. in the deploy user's crontab:\n\n```sh\n15 2 * * * BACKUP_REMOTE=backup@backup-host:/srv/qsell/<id>/ $APP_DIR/scripts/backup-instance.sh $DEPLOY_PATH >> $APP_DIR/backup.log 2>&1\n```\n\nKeep backups off the host and test a restore regularly. PostgreSQL 18 uses\n`/var/lib/postgresql` as its volume root; do not reuse an older major version's data\nvolume without a planned `pg_upgrade` or dump/restore.\n\n### 6.5 Add a domain, move, or decommission\n\n- **Add a hostname:** add it to `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, publish a new\n  release, extend the Nginx `server_name`/certificate, redeploy.\n- **Second installation on the same host:** a new config file with a new\n  `INSTANCE_ID`, `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` and a **different `EDGE_HTTP_PORT`**; repeat phases\n  A, B, D–I (skip C).\n- **Decommission:** `dc down -v` (deletes that installation's data — back up first),\n  remove its directory, Nginx site, certificate (`certbot delete`) and GitHub\n  Environment.\n\n### 6.6 Capacity\n\nEach installation is an independent single-host Compose stack — not a cluster.\nTune `APP_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `POSTGRES_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT`, the CPU\nsettings, DB pool size and `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` for the host. The worker has a\ncontainer healthcheck (`scripts/worker-healthcheck.mjs`).\n\n## 7. Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom (workflow / server output)                                | Cause and fix                                                                                          |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `Set this environment's PUBLIC_DOMAIN Actions variable`           | Must be an Environment **variable** (not a secret) on the right Environment, bare hostname. Same for the other six variables. |\n| `Invalid instance id`                                             | `INSTANCE_ID` allows only `a-z 0-9 -` (no underscore). The folder name may differ; the Environment may not. |\n| `Unknown MEDIA_DRIVER '…'`                                        | Typo in `.env.runtime` (`cloudinary`/`local` only). Nothing was deployed.                              |\n| `MEDIA_DRIVER=cloudinary but … missing Cloudinary credentials`    | Add `CLOUDINARY_URL` (or all three parts) to `.env.runtime`.                                           |\n| `No successful Release build pipeline exists for …`               | SHA wasn't built on `release` (PR or failed publish). Leave SHA empty or pick one from a green run.    |\n| Workflow not listed in the Actions UI                             | `deploy-instance.yml` isn't on `main` yet ([section 3](#3-one-time-repository-setup)).                 |\n| `Missing …/.env.runtime` / `postgres_password`                    | Run `provision-instance.sh` first (phase D) and check `DEPLOY_PATH` matches.                           |\n| `DATABASE_URL must address … host db`                             | `.env.runtime` must use `@db:5432`. Never share a database between installations.                      |\n| SSH `Permission denied (publickey)`                               | Public key not in `~$DEPLOY_USER/.ssh/authorized_keys` (the account has no password; use `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` in phase C). |\n| Host key / `known_hosts` error                                    | `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS` must be for the same name/IP as `DEPLOY_HOST`; re-run phase F.                    |\n| `denied` pulling images                                           | `GHCR_READ_TOKEN`/`GHCR_USERNAME` wrong or token lacks package read access.                            |\n| Health check fails, stack rolled back                             | `dc logs app` (bad env value, DB, migration). Fix and redeploy. First deploys have nothing to roll back to. |\n| `Failed server action` / origin errors in the browser             | Domain missing from `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` at **build** time. Add it, publish a new release, redeploy. |\n| HTTPS check warns \"Nginx does not include …\"                      | Expected on the first deploy: run phase H.                                                             |\n| `certbot` fails                                                   | DNS not pointing here, port 80 blocked, or Cloudflare proxy on during issuance.                        |\n| `nginx -t` fails after phase H                                    | Run `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run`, compare with `/etc/nginx/sites-available/<id>`; fix and re-run.   |\n| Run is red after a healthy deploy                                 | Look at the *last* failing step: the media smoke test (Cloudinary credentials) is deliberately last and non-blocking for traffic. |\n\n## 8. Nothing here is tied to one\nserver: every host-specific value lives in a single **instance config file**, and\nthe scripts and GitHub workflows read it.\n\n- [1. How it works](#1-how-it-works)\n- [2. The parameter sheet](#2-the-parameter-sheet)\n- [3. One-time repository setup](#3-one-time-repository-setup)\n- [4. New server: step by step](#4-new-server-step-by-step)\n- [5. Releasing](#5-releasing)\n- [6. Operations](#6-operations)\n- [7. Troubleshooting](#7-troubleshooting)\n- [8. Image uploads (media storage)](#8-image-uploads-media-storage)\n\n## 1. How it works\n\n```\n you ──PR/merge──▶ release branch ──▶ \"Release build pipeline\"\n                                        validate (typecheck, tests, build)\n                                        publish immutable GHCR images:\n                                          sha-<commit> · worker-<commit> · migrator-<commit>\n                                        (deploys NOTHING)\n\n you ──run manually──▶ \"Deploy release to instance\" (pick Environment, SHA optional)\n                          │ SSH (per-Environment key, pinned host key)\n                          ▼\n   ┌────────────────────── one server, one installation ──────────────────────┐\n   │ Internet ─▶ Cloudflare (optional) ─▶ Nginx :80/:443 (TLS, host-owned)    │\n   │              ─▶ Caddy 127.0.0.1:$EDGE_HTTP_PORT ─▶ app :3069             │\n   │ Docker Compose project $COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:                            │\n   │   db (Postgres 18) · app (Next.js) · worker (Graphile) · caddy · migrate │\n   │ Files: $DEPLOY_PATH/.env.runtime  secrets/postgres_password             │\n   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nPrinciples:\n\n- **Build once, deploy many.** Images are shared; runtime configuration is not.\n- **Nothing deploys by itself.** A merge publishes images. A person picks which\n  installation gets which release.\n- **Isolation.** Each installation has its own database, secrets, volumes, domain,\n  Compose project and loopback port. Deploying one never touches another. Never\n  point two installations at one database.\n- **Secrets stay on the host.** `.env.runtime` and the Postgres password are\n  created on the server and never pass through GitHub. GitHub holds only what is\n  needed to reach and pull: an SSH key, the pinned host key and a read-only\n  registry token.\n- **Safe rollouts.** Order is: validate → pull → migrate → replace → health check.\n  A failed migration stops before anything is replaced; a failed health check\n  rolls app, worker and Caddy back to the previous images.\n\n## 2. The parameter sheet\n\nEverything that differs per server is one of these. Copy\n`deploy/instance.env.example` to `deploy/instances/<INSTANCE_ID>.env` (git-ignored)\nand fill it in. All scripts accept `--config <file>`, and any value can instead be\npassed as an environment variable (which wins over the file).\n\n| Parameter              | Required | Default                           | Meaning / rules                                                                                    |\n| ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `INSTANCE_ID`          | yes      | –                                 | Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (max 40). Becomes the GitHub Environment and Nginx snippet name. |\n| `PUBLIC_DOMAIN`        | yes      | –                                 | Bare hostname (`shop.example.com`). No `https://`, slash or port.                                  |\n| `DEPLOY_HOST`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | IP/DNS GitHub Actions SSHs to. \\\\*GitHub step only.                                                 |\n| `DEPLOY_USER`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | Account that owns the instance dir and runs Docker (`setup-server.sh` creates it as `APP_USER`).   |\n| `APP_DIR`              | no       | `/opt/qsell`                      | Root for all installations on the host.                                                            |\n| `DEPLOY_PATH`          | no       | `$APP_DIR/instances/$INSTANCE_ID` | Absolute path; letters, digits, `/ _ -` only. Its folder name need not equal `INSTANCE_ID`.        |\n| `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` | no       | `qsell-$INSTANCE_ID`              | Namespaces containers/volumes. Unique per installation on a host. **Never change on a live one.**  |\n| `EDGE_HTTP_PORT`       | no       | `8080`                            | Loopback port for Caddy (1024–65535). Unique per installation on a host.                           |\n| `ADMIN_EMAIL`          | yes      | –                                 | Initial super-admin login.                                                                         |\n| `MEDIA_DRIVER`         | no       | `local`                           | `local` or `cloudinary` (see [section 8](#8-image-uploads-media-storage)).                         |\n| `CERT_EMAIL`           | yes      | –                                 | Let's Encrypt expiry notices.                                                                      |\n| `GITHUB_REPO`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | `owner/name` of the repository.                                                                    |\n| `GHCR_USERNAME`        | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | GitHub user whose token can read the private images.                                               |\n| `SSH_KEY_FILE`         | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | Path (on your machine) of the passphrase-less deploy key for this installation.                    |\n\nWhere each value ends up:\n\n| GitHub Environment **variable** | From                                                         |\n| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `DEPLOY_HOST` `DEPLOY_USER`     | same names                                                   |\n| `DEPLOY_PATH`                   | same name (derived if unset)                                 |\n| `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`          | same name (derived if unset)                                 |\n| `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` `EDGE_HTTP_PORT` `GHCR_USERNAME` | same names                                  |\n\n| GitHub Environment **secret** | Source                                                       |\n| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `DEPLOY_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`      | Releasing\n\n1. Open a pull request into `release`. CI installs locked dependencies, migrates a\n   disposable database, typechecks, runs `pnpm test` (including database integration\n   tests), `pnpm media:verify`, and a production build. Lint is not gated yet.\n2. Merge. `Release build pipeline` publishes the three images for that commit.\n3. Run **Deploy release to instance** for each installation you want to update.\n   Leave the SHA empty for the newest build, or paste a full 40-character SHA to\n   deploy or roll back to a specific one (it must have a successful build).\n\nSafety behaviour: a failed migration stops before anything is replaced. A failed\nhealth check **rolls back** app, worker and Caddy to the previous image set\n(`.env.deploy.previous`). **The database schema is never rolled back**, so migrations\nmust be backward-compatible with the previous release (add columns/tables first;\ndrop or rename in a later release). Replacing the app container causes a brief\ninterruption. One deploy per Environment runs at a time.\n\n## 6. Operations\n\nAll commands run on the server in `$DEPLOY_PATH`:\n\n```sh\nalias dc='docker compose --env-file .env.deploy -f compose.production.yaml'\n```\n\n### 6.1 Status and logs\n\n```sh\ndc ps                    # app/worker/db/caddy and health\ndc logs -f app worker\n```\n\n### 6.2 Roll back by hand\n\nRun the deploy workflow with the previous good SHA (preferred). Emergency, on the\nhost: `cp .env.deploy.previous .env.deploy && dc up -d`.\n\n### 6.3 Change configuration\n\nEdit `.env.runtime` (keep mode `600`), then `dc up -d app worker`. Never edit\n`COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, the database password or `DATABASE_URL` on a live instance.\n\n### 6.4 Backups\n\n`scripts/backup-instance.sh $DEPLOY_PATH` dumps Postgres and the local media volume,\nprunes after `BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS` (default 14) and rsyncs to `BACKUP_REMOTE` when set.\nSchedule it per instance, e.g. in the deploy user's crontab:\n\n```sh\n15 2 * * * BACKUP_REMOTE=backup@backup-host:/srv/qsell/<id>/ $APP_DIR/scripts/backup-instance.sh $DEPLOY_PATH >> $APP_DIR/backup.log 2>&1\n```\n\nKeep backups off the host and test a restore regularly. PostgreSQL 18 uses\n`/var/lib/postgresql` as its volume root; do not reuse an older major version's data\nvolume without a planned `pg_upgrade` or dump/restore.\n\n### 6.5 Add a domain, move, or decommission\n\n- **Add a hostname:** add it to `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, publish a new\n  release, extend the Nginx `server_name`/certificate, redeploy.\n- **Second installation on the same host:** a new config file with a new\n  `INSTANCE_ID`, `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` and a **different `EDGE_HTTP_PORT`**; repeat phases\n  A, B, D–I (skip C).\n- **Decommission:** `dc down -v` (deletes that installation's data — back up first),\n  remove its directory, Nginx site, certificate (`certbot delete`) and GitHub\n  Environment.\n\n### 6.6 Capacity\n\nEach installation is an independent single-host Compose stack — not a cluster.\nTune `APP_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `POSTGRES_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT`, the CPU\nsettings, DB pool size and `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` for the host. The worker has a\ncontainer healthcheck (`scripts/worker-healthcheck.mjs`).\n\n## 7. Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom (workflow / server output)                                | Cause and fix                                                                                          |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `Set this environment's PUBLIC_DOMAIN Actions variable`           | Must be an Environment **variable** (not a secret) on the right Environment, bare hostname. Same for the other six variables. |\n| `Invalid instance id`                                             | `INSTANCE_ID` allows only `a-z 0-9 -` (no underscore). The folder name may differ; the Environment may not. |\n| `Unknown MEDIA_DRIVER '…'`                                        | Typo in `.env.runtime` (`cloudinary`/`local` only). Nothing was deployed.                              |\n| `MEDIA_DRIVER=cloudinary but … missing Cloudinary credentials`    | Add `CLOUDINARY_URL` (or all three parts) to `.env.runtime`.                                           |\n| `No successful Release build pipeline exists for …`               | SHA wasn't built on `release` (PR or failed publish). Leave SHA empty or pick one from a green run.    |\n| Workflow not listed in the Actions UI                             | `deploy-instance.yml` isn't on `main` yet ([section 3](#3-one-time-repository-setup)).                 |\n| `Missing …/.env.runtime` / `postgres_password`                    | Run `provision-instance.sh` first (phase D) and check `DEPLOY_PATH` matches.                           |\n| `DATABASE_URL must address … host db`                             | `.env.runtime` must use `@db:5432`. Never share a database between installations.                      |\n| SSH `Permission denied (publickey)`                               | Public key not in `~$DEPLOY_USER/.ssh/authorized_keys` (the account has no password; use `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` in phase C). |\n| Host key / `known_hosts` error                                    | `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS` must be for the same name/IP as `DEPLOY_HOST`; re-run phase F.                    |\n| `denied` pulling images                                           | `GHCR_READ_TOKEN`/`GHCR_USERNAME` wrong or token lacks package read access.                            |\n| Health check fails, stack rolled back                             | `dc logs app` (bad env value, DB, migration). Fix and redeploy. First deploys have nothing to roll back to. |\n| `Failed server action` / origin errors in the browser             | Domain missing from `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` at **build** time. Add it, publish a new release, redeploy. |\n| HTTPS check warns \"Nginx does not include …\"                      | Expected on the first deploy: run phase H.                                                             |\n| `certbot` fails                                                   | DNS not pointing here, port 80 blocked, or Cloudflare proxy on during issuance.                        |\n| `nginx -t` fails after phase H                                    | Run `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run`, compare with `/etc/nginx/sites-available/<id>`; fix and re-run.   |\n| Run is red after a healthy deploy                                 | Look at the *last* failing step: the media smoke test (Cloudinary credentials) is deliberately last and non-blocking for traffic. |\n\n## 8. Nothing here is tied to one\nserver: every host-specific value lives in a single **instance config file**, and\nthe scripts and GitHub workflows read it.\n\n- [1. How it works](#1-how-it-works)\n- [2. The parameter sheet](#2-the-parameter-sheet)\n- [3. One-time repository setup](#3-one-time-repository-setup)\n- [4. New server: step by step](#4-new-server-step-by-step)\n- [5. Releasing](#5-releasing)\n- [6. Operations](#6-operations)\n- [7. Troubleshooting](#7-troubleshooting)\n- [8. Image uploads (media storage)](#8-image-uploads-media-storage)\n\n## 1. How it works\n\n```\n you ──PR/merge──▶ release branch ──▶ \"Release build pipeline\"\n                                        validate (typecheck, tests, build)\n                                        publish immutable GHCR images:\n                                          sha-<commit> · worker-<commit> · migrator-<commit>\n                                        (deploys NOTHING)\n\n you ──run manually──▶ \"Deploy release to instance\" (pick Environment, SHA optional)\n                          │ SSH (per-Environment key, pinned host key)\n                          ▼\n   ┌────────────────────── one server, one installation ──────────────────────┐\n   │ Internet ─▶ Cloudflare (optional) ─▶ Nginx :80/:443 (TLS, host-owned)    │\n   │              ─▶ Caddy 127.0.0.1:$EDGE_HTTP_PORT ─▶ app :3069             │\n   │ Docker Compose project $COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:                            │\n   │   db (Postgres 18) · app (Next.js) · worker (Graphile) · caddy · migrate │\n   │ Files: $DEPLOY_PATH/.env.runtime  secrets/postgres_password             │\n   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nPrinciples:\n\n- **Build once, deploy many.** Images are shared; runtime configuration is not.\n- **Nothing deploys by itself.** A merge publishes images. A person picks which\n  installation gets which release.\n- **Isolation.** Each installation has its own database, secrets, volumes, domain,\n  Compose project and loopback port. Deploying one never touches another. Never\n  point two installations at one database.\n- **Secrets stay on the host.** `.env.runtime` and the Postgres password are\n  created on the server and never pass through GitHub. GitHub holds only what is\n  needed to reach and pull: an SSH key, the pinned host key and a read-only\n  registry token.\n- **Safe rollouts.** Order is: validate → pull → migrate → replace → health check.\n  A failed migration stops before anything is replaced; a failed health check\n  rolls app, worker and Caddy back to the previous images.\n\n## 2. The parameter sheet\n\nEverything that differs per server is one of these. Copy\n`deploy/instance.env.example` to `deploy/instances/<INSTANCE_ID>.env` (git-ignored)\nand fill it in. All scripts accept `--config <file>`, and any value can instead be\npassed as an environment variable (which wins over the file).\n\n| Parameter              | Required | Default                           | Meaning / rules                                                                                    |\n| ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `INSTANCE_ID`          | yes      | –                                 | Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (max 40). Becomes the GitHub Environment and Nginx snippet name. |\n| `PUBLIC_DOMAIN`        | yes      | –                                 | Bare hostname (`shop.example.com`). No `https://`, slash or port.                                  |\n| `DEPLOY_HOST`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | IP/DNS GitHub Actions SSHs to. \\\\*GitHub step only.                                                 |\n| `DEPLOY_USER`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | Account that owns the instance dir and runs Docker (`setup-server.sh` creates it as `APP_USER`).   |\n| `APP_DIR`              | no       | `/opt/qsell`                      | Root for all installations on the host.                                                            |\n| `DEPLOY_PATH`          | no       | `$APP_DIR/instances/$INSTANCE_ID` | Absolute path; letters, digits, `/ _ -` only. Its folder name need not equal `INSTANCE_ID`.        |\n| `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` | no       | `qsell-$INSTANCE_ID`              | Namespaces containers/volumes. Unique per installation on a host. **Never change on a live one.**  |\n| `EDGE_HTTP_PORT`       | no       | `8080`                            | Loopback port for Caddy (1024–65535). Unique per installation on a host.                           |\n| `ADMIN_EMAIL`          | yes      | –                                 | Initial super-admin login.                                                                         |\n| `MEDIA_DRIVER`         | no       | `local`                           | `local` or `cloudinary` (see [section 8](#8-image-uploads-media-storage)).                         |\n| `CERT_EMAIL`           | yes      | –                                 | Let's Encrypt expiry notices.                                                                      |\n| `GITHUB_REPO`          | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | `owner/name` of the repository.                                                                    |\n| `GHCR_USERNAME`        | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | GitHub user whose token can read the private images.                                               |\n| `SSH_KEY_FILE`         | yes\\\\*   | –                                 | Path (on your machine) of the passphrase-less deploy key for this installation.                    |\n\nWhere each value ends up:\n\n| GitHub Environment **variable** | From                                                         |\n| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `DEPLOY_HOST` `DEPLOY_USER`     | same names                                                   |\n| `DEPLOY_PATH`                   | same name (derived if unset)                                 |\n| `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`          | same name (derived if unset)                                 |\n| `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` `EDGE_HTTP_PORT` `GHCR_USERNAME` | same names                                  |\n\n| GitHub Environment **secret** | Source                                                       |\n| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `DEPLOY_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`      | contents of `SSH_KEY_FILE`                                   |\n| `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS`          | `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 $DEPLOY_HOST` (fingerprint confirmed) |\n| `GHCR_READ_TOKEN`             | fine-grained token with read access to the package           |\n\nOn the server, per installation: `$DEPLOY_PATH/.env.runtime` (app configuration and\nsecrets) and `$DEPLOY_PATH/secrets/postgres_password`, both mode `600`.\n\n## 3. One-time repository setup\n\nDone once per repository, not per server.\n\n1. Merge `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml` **and** `deploy-instance.yml` into `release`\n   *and* `main`. GitHub lists a manually-run workflow only when it exists on the\n   default branch (`main`); the deploy job itself refuses to run from any ref but\n   `release`.\n2. Repository **variable** `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`: comma-separated list of\n   **every** installation's domain. It is compiled into the shared image, so add a\n   new domain here and publish a fresh release build *before* deploying to it.\n   Optional: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`; secret `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` for source maps.\n3. Create a fine-grained GitHub token with read access to the repository's\n   package (GHCR). Keep it ready for `GHCR_READ_TOKEN`.\n4. Install the GitHub CLI (`gh`) on your machine and run `gh auth login` as someone\n   with admin rights on the repository.\n\n## 4. New server: step by step\n\nVariables below are shown as `$NAME`; they all come from your config file. Phases\nmarked **laptop** run on your machine, **root** / **deploy** on the server.\n\n### Phase A — DNS (laptop)\n\nCreate an `A` record for `$PUBLIC_DOMAIN` pointing to the server's public IP. With\nCloudflare, leave the record **DNS only** (grey cloud) until the certificate is\nissued, then proxy it and set SSL mode to **Full (strict)**.\n\n### Phase B — Deploy key (laptop)\n\n```sh\nscripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/<id>.env \\\\\n  --generate-key --dry-run\n```\n\nThis creates `$SSH_KEY_FILE` (ed25519, no passphrase — `webfactory/ssh-agent`\ncannot use passphrase-protected keys) and prints its **public** half. Do not reuse\nyour personal key.\n\n### Phase C — Bootstrap the host (root, on the server)\n\n```sh\ngit clone https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPO /tmp/qsell && cd /tmp/qsell\nsudo APP_USER=$DEPLOY_USER APP_DIR=$APP_DIR \\\\\n     SSH_PUBLIC_KEY='ssh-ed25519 AAAA… qsell-actions-<id>' \\\\\n     ./scripts/setup-server.sh\n```\n\nInstalls Docker Engine + Compose/Buildx (log rotation, live-restore), creates the\ndeploy account with a **locked password** (so `ssh-copy-id` cannot work — hence\n`SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`), creates `$APP_DIR/instances`, and opens UFW for 22/80/443.\nSupports Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04. Docker group membership is root-equivalent:\nrestrict the account to trusted operators. Log in again so the group applies, and\nreboot if Ubuntu reports a pending kernel update.\n\nCheck: `ssh -i $SSH_KEY_FILE $DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST 'id -un && docker ps'`.\n\n### Phase D — Create the instance (deploy user, on the server)\n\nCopy your config file to the server (it holds no secrets), then:\n\n```sh\ncd /tmp/qsell\nscripts/provision-instance.sh --config /path/to/<id>.env\n```\n\nCreates `$DEPLOY_PATH` and `secrets/`, generates a random Postgres password and all\napplication secrets, and writes `.env.runtime` (mode `600`). It prompts for the admin\npassword (or generates one and shows it once). It will **not overwrite** an existing\n`.env.runtime` or password — regenerating the DB password after the volume exists\nwould lock the app out of its own database.\n\n- Extra settings (SMTP, payment providers, Cloudinary…): put `KEY=VALUE` lines in a\n  file and pass `EXTRA_ENV_FILE=…`, or edit `.env.runtime` afterwards.\n- **Back up** `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` / `PAYMENT_DATA_KEY` somewhere safe; losing them\n  makes encrypted data unreadable.\n\n### Phase E — Nginx and TLS (root, on the server)\n\n```sh\nsudo scripts/setup-nginx-site.sh --config /path/to/<id>.env\n```\n\nInstalls Nginx + certbot, obtains the certificate through the port-80 webroot\nchallenge, writes `/etc/nginx/sites-available/$INSTANCE_ID`, enables it and reloads.\nUntil the first deploy, `/` answers `503`. Preview without changing anything:\n`--dry-run`. Certificates renew automatically (`certbot.timer`).\n\n### Phase F — GitHub Environment (laptop)\n\n```sh\nscripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/<id>.env\n```\n\nCreates the Environment named `$INSTANCE_ID`, sets the seven variables and three\nsecrets from [section 2](#2-the-parameter-sheet), shows the host-key fingerprint and\nasks you to confirm it matches the server (`ssh-keygen -lf\n/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`) before trusting it, and prompts (hidden) for the\nregistry token. Add reviewers to the Environment for higher-risk targets. Remember\n[section 3](#3-one-time-repository-setup) step 2: the new domain must be in\n`SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` and a release must have been built **after** adding it.\n\n### Phase G — First deploy\n\nGitHub → Actions → **Deploy release to instance** → *Run workflow* on branch\n`release`, Environment `$INSTANCE_ID`, SHA empty (= newest successful release build).\n\nThe workflow: validates the Environment → resolves the release → SSHes in → refuses\nunless `.env.runtime` and the Postgres password exist and `DATABASE_URL` uses host\n`db` → validates media settings → pulls images → runs migrations → starts the stack →\nwrites `$DEPLOY_PATH/deploy/nginx/$INSTANCE_ID.conf` → waits for a healthy `/api/health`\n→ checks `media.uploadsReady`. The final HTTPS check only **warns** on this first run,\nbecause Nginx does not include the snippet yet.\n\n### Phase H — Switch the site on (root, on the server)\n\n```sh\nsudo scripts/setup-nginx-site.sh --config /path/to/<id>.env --no-cert\n```\n\nRe-running detects the generated snippet, replaces the `503` placeholder with the\ninclude, validates (`nginx -t`) and reloads.\n\n### Phase I — Go-live checklist\n\n- [ ] `curl -s https://$PUBLIC_DOMAIN/api/health` → `\"status\":\"healthy\"`, `uploadsReady:true`\n- [ ] Log in at `/admin` as `$ADMIN_EMAIL`; change the initial password\n- [ ] Upload a product image (and, for Cloudinary, check the deploy's media step was green)\n- [ ] Cloudflare proxy on, SSL **Full (strict)** (if used)\n- [ ] Backups scheduled and a restore tested ([6.4](#64-backups))\n- [ ] `sudo reboot` once if a kernel update was pending; confirm the stack returns\n\n## 5. Releasing\n\n1. Open a pull request into `release`. CI installs locked dependencies, migrates a\n   disposable database, typechecks, runs `pnpm test` (including database integration\n   tests), `pnpm media:verify`, and a production build. Lint is not gated yet.\n2. Merge. `Release build pipeline` publishes the three images for that commit.\n3. Run **Deploy release to instance** for each installation you want to update.\n   Leave the SHA empty for the newest build, or paste a full 40-character SHA to\n   deploy or roll back to a specific one (it must have a successful build).\n\nSafety behaviour: a failed migration stops before anything is replaced. A failed\nhealth check **rolls back** app, worker and Caddy to the previous image set\n(`.env.deploy.previous`). **The database schema is never rolled back**, so migrations\nmust be backward-compatible with the previous release (add columns/tables first;\ndrop or rename in a later release). Replacing the app container causes a brief\ninterruption. One deploy per Environment runs at a time.\n\n## 6. Operations\n\nAll commands run on the server in `$DEPLOY_PATH`:\n\n```sh\nalias dc='docker compose --env-file .env.deploy -f compose.production.yaml'\n```\n\n### 6.1 Status and logs\n\n```sh\ndc ps                    # app/worker/db/caddy and health\ndc logs -f app worker\n```\n\n### 6.2 Roll back by hand\n\nRun the deploy workflow with the previous good SHA (preferred). Emergency, on the\nhost: `cp .env.deploy.previous .env.deploy && dc up -d`.\n\n### 6.3 Change configuration\n\nEdit `.env.runtime` (keep mode `600`), then `dc up -d app worker`. Never edit\n`COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, the database password or `DATABASE_URL` on a live instance.\n\n### 6.4 Backups\n\n`scripts/backup-instance.sh $DEPLOY_PATH` dumps Postgres and the local media volume,\nprunes after `BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS` (default 14) and rsyncs to `BACKUP_REMOTE` when set.\nSchedule it per instance, e.g. in the deploy user's crontab:\n\n```sh\n15 2 * * * BACKUP_REMOTE=backup@backup-host:/srv/qsell/<id>/ $APP_DIR/scripts/backup-instance.sh $DEPLOY_PATH >> $APP_DIR/backup.log 2>&1\n```\n\nKeep backups off the host and test a restore regularly. PostgreSQL 18 uses\n`/var/lib/postgresql` as its volume root; do not reuse an older major version's data\nvolume without a planned `pg_upgrade` or dump/restore.\n\n### 6.5 Add a domain, move, or decommission\n\n- **Add a hostname:** add it to `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, publish a new\n  release, extend the Nginx `server_name`/certificate, redeploy.\n- **Second installation on the same host:** a new config file with a new\n  `INSTANCE_ID`, `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` and a **different `EDGE_HTTP_PORT`**; repeat phases\n  A, B, D–I (skip C).\n- **Decommission:** `dc down -v` (deletes that installation's data — back up first),\n  remove its directory, Nginx site, certificate (`certbot delete`) and GitHub\n  Environment.\n\n### 6.6 Capacity\n\nEach installation is an independent single-host Compose stack — not a cluster.\nTune `APP_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `POSTGRES_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `WORKER_MEMORY_LIMIT`, the CPU\nsettings, DB pool size and `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` for the host. The worker has a\ncontainer healthcheck (`scripts/worker-healthcheck.mjs`).\n\n## 7. Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom (workflow / server output)                                | Cause and fix                                                                                          |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `Set this environment's PUBLIC_DOMAIN Actions variable`           | Must be an Environment **variable** (not a secret) on the right Environment, bare hostname. Same for the other six variables. |\n| `Invalid instance id`                                             | `INSTANCE_ID` allows only `a-z 0-9 -` (no underscore). The folder name may differ; the Environment may not. |\n| `Unknown MEDIA_DRIVER '…'`                                        | Typo in `.env.runtime` (`cloudinary`/`local` only). Nothing was deployed.                              |\n| `MEDIA_DRIVER=cloudinary but … missing Cloudinary credentials`    | Add `CLOUDINARY_URL` (or all three parts) to `.env.runtime`.                                           |\n| `No successful Release build pipeline exists for …`               | SHA wasn't built on `release` (PR or failed publish). Leave SHA empty or pick one from a green run.    |\n| Workflow not listed in the Actions UI                             | `deploy-instance.yml` isn't on `main` yet ([section 3](#3-one-time-repository-setup)).                 |\n| `Missing …/.env.runtime` / `postgres_password`                    | Run `provision-instance.sh` first (phase D) and check `DEPLOY_PATH` matches.                           |\n| `DATABASE_URL must address … host db`                             | `.env.runtime` must use `@db:5432`. Never share a database between installations.                      |\n| SSH `Permission denied (publickey)`                               | Public key not in `~$DEPLOY_USER/.ssh/authorized_keys` (the account has no password; use `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` in phase C). |\n| Host key / `known_hosts` error                                    | `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS` must be for the same name/IP as `DEPLOY_HOST`; re-run phase F.                    |\n| `denied` pulling images                                           | `GHCR_READ_TOKEN`/`GHCR_USERNAME` wrong or token lacks package read access.                            |\n| Health check fails, stack rolled back                             | `dc logs app` (bad env value, DB, migration). Fix and redeploy. First deploys have nothing to roll back to. |\n| `Failed server action` / origin errors in the browser             | Domain missing from `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` at **build** time. Add it, publish a new release, redeploy. |\n| HTTPS check warns \"Nginx does not include …\"                      | Expected on the first deploy: run phase H.                                                             |\n| `certbot` fails                                                   | DNS not pointing here, port 80 blocked, or Cloudflare proxy on during issuance.                        |\n| `nginx -t` fails after phase H                                    | Run `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run`, compare with `/etc/nginx/sites-available/<id>`; fix and re-run.   |\n| Run is red after a healthy deploy                                 | Look at the *last* failing step: the media smoke test (Cloudinary credentials) is deliberately last and non-blocking for traffic. |\n\n## 8. Image uploads (media storage)\n\n'''\nmedia=media.replace(\"## Image uploads (media storage)\\n\\n\",\"\",1)\nopen('DEPLOYMENT.md','w').write(new+media)\nPYEOF\nnpx prettier --write DEPLOYMENT.md >/dev/null && npx prettier --check DEPLOYMENT.md | tail -1; wc -l DEPLOYMENT.md; grep -n \"new-shop\" DEPLOYMENT.md | head"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

{"parentUuid":"f56ef401-2421-40aa-8f3d-4fcad1c3bb1a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg433aAgedWjJ7DNgNbJC","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've rewritten `DEPLOYMENT.md` as an end-to-end runbook and added scripts so each new server is driven by one config file. I tested the scripts locally, but I haven't run them on a real server or against GitHub (see \"Not verified\" below). Nothing is committed.\n\n## How it works now\n\nYou fill in one file per server, `deploy/instances/<id>.env`, and every script reads it. The template is `deploy/instance.env.example`, and the real copies are git-ignored. A value passed as an environment variable overrides the file. Defaults are derived from `INSTANCE_ID`: the directory is `$APP_DIR/instances/<id>`, the project name is `qsell-<id>`, and the port is 8080. There are no hardcoded users, IPs or domains.\n\n| Step | Script | Where it runs |\n|---|---|---|\n| Create the deploy key | `configure-github-environment.sh --generate-key` | your laptop |\n| Bootstrap the host | `setup-server.sh` (now takes `APP_USER`, `APP_DIR` and `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`) | server, as root |\n| Create the instance directory, secrets and `.env.runtime` | `provision-instance.sh` (new) | server, as the deploy user |\n| Nginx, certificate and vhost | `setup-nginx-site.sh` (new) | server, as root |\n| Create the GitHub Environment (7 variables, 3 secrets) | `configure-github-environment.sh` (new) | your laptop |\n| Deploy | the workflow, with the SHA optional | GitHub |\n| Switch the site on | `setup-nginx-site.sh --no-cert` (re-run) | server, as root |\n\n## What the runbook covers\n\n`DEPLOYMENT.md` now has an architecture diagram, the full parameter table (what each value means, its rules, its default, and where it ends up in GitHub), one-time repository setup, phases A to I with a go-live checklist, the release flow, operations, and a troubleshooting table. The troubleshooting table lists every error we actually hit: the missing `PUBLIC_DOMAIN`, the underscore in the instance id, the `MEDIA_DRIVER` typo, the locked-account `ssh-copy-id` problem, the unset `RELEASE_SHA`, and the missing Nginx include.\n\n## Mistakes the scripts now prevent\n\n- **Config checked before CI.** They validate your values with the same rules the deploy workflow uses, so a bad `INSTANCE_ID` or domain fails before you run anything on the server.\n- **Secrets never overwritten.** `provision-instance.sh` refuses to replace an existing `.env.runtime` or Postgres password. Regenerating the password after the database volume exists would lock the app out of its own database.\n- **Host key confirmed.** `configure-github-environment.sh` shows the host key fingerprint and asks you to confirm it before trusting it.\n- **Key install fixed.** `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` installs the deploy key directly, which replaces the `ssh-copy-id` step that couldn't work.\n- **Existing hosts still work.** I changed the default deploy user from `creame` to `deploy`. If you rely on the old default, pass `APP_USER` explicitly.\n\n## What I tested\n\n- **Provisioning:** I ran `provision-instance.sh` into a scratch directory. It created the files with mode 600, left the second run untouched, and rejected a bad instance id and a `https://` domain. The Cloudinary variant warned about missing credentials, and `EXTRA_ENV_FILE` was appended.\n- **Nginx and GitHub:** `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run` renders the vhost. `configure-github-environment.sh --dry-run` printed the right `gh` calls.\n- **A bug the tests caught:** an apostrophe broke the closing summary of `provision-instance.sh`. I fixed it.\n\n## Not verified\n\n- **Real server:** nothing has run on an actual server. The `apt` installs, the certbot webroot flow, and the include swap in phase H follow the setup we ran by hand, but they're untested as scripts.\n- **GitHub:** the `gh` writes (creating the Environment, setting variables and secrets) have only been dry-run.\n- **Shellcheck:** not installed here, so only `bash -n` was run.\n\nI'd run `setup-nginx-site.sh` on your next server with `--dry-run` first. It also doesn't touch your live `san-marina` instance."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":495,"cache_read_input_tokens":208583,"output_tokens":1509,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":495,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1509,"cache_read_input_tokens":208583,"cache_creation_input_tokens":495,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":495},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"532b20d2-d78e-4919-a4a1-97401efc1553","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011Cg433ZjPLaWrkMhUYV8DC","requestRef":"6a3d452d-72ca-48eb-9eca-01def580bcd3","requestedModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"14903535-6ef0-41e5-9383-f3f79214a97a","timestamp":"2026-10-15T12:38:38.746Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"166f5a26-a325-49b5-bd9f-cdd3ea150cc4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell","sessionId":"166f5a26-a325-49b5-bd9f-cdd3ea150cc4","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"feat/finance-f4"}
