{"parentUuid":"e237eb93-9c1e-4cbd-a4ed-b0d6ed598077","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg43UW8HiSFw8DaCq5LAA","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VAFXDZkTSVyDSUV8ev3wNu","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell/docs/deployment/new-server-flow.md","content":"# New-server deployment flow: summary\n\nThe full runbook is [DEPLOYMENT.md](../../DEPLOYMENT.md). This page summarises the\nconfig-file-driven flow and what the scripts do.\n\n## How it works\n\nYou fill in one file per server, `deploy/instances/<id>.env`, and every script reads\nit. The template is `deploy/instance.env.example`; real copies are git-ignored.\n\n- A value passed as an environment variable overrides the file.\n- Defaults are derived from `INSTANCE_ID`:\n  - directory: `$APP_DIR/instances/<id>` (`APP_DIR` defaults to `/opt/qsell`)\n  - Compose project name: `qsell-<id>`\n  - loopback port: `8080`\n- There are no hardcoded users, IPs or domains.\n\n| Step                                                    | Script                                                                          | Where it runs              |\n| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |\n| Create the deploy key                                   | `configure-github-environment.sh --generate-key`                                | your laptop                |\n| Bootstrap the host                                      | `setup-server.sh` (takes `APP_USER`, `APP_DIR` and `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`)            | server, as root            |\n| Create the instance directory, secrets and `.env.runtime` | `provision-instance.sh`                                                         | server, as the deploy user |\n| Nginx, certificate and vhost                            | `setup-nginx-site.sh`                                                           | server, as root            |\n| Create the GitHub Environment (7 variables, 3 secrets)  | `configure-github-environment.sh`                                               | your laptop                |\n| Deploy                                                  | the \"Deploy release to instance\" workflow (the SHA is optional)                 | GitHub                     |\n| Switch the site on                                      | `setup-nginx-site.sh --no-cert` (re-run after the first deploy)                 | server, as root            |\n\n## What `DEPLOYMENT.md` covers\n\n- An architecture diagram.\n- The full parameter table: what each value means, its rules, its default, and where\n  it ends up in GitHub.\n- One-time repository setup.\n- Phases A to I for a new server, with a go-live checklist.\n- The release flow, rollback behaviour and operations (logs, backups, adding a domain,\n  decommissioning).\n- A troubleshooting table covering the errors hit while setting up `san-marina`:\n  - the missing `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` variable\n  - the underscore in the instance id\n  - the `MEDIA_DRIVER` typo\n  - the locked-account `ssh-copy-id` problem\n  - the unset `RELEASE_SHA`\n  - the missing Nginx include\n\n## Mistakes the scripts now prevent\n\n- **Config checked before CI.** They validate your values with the same rules the\n  deploy workflow uses, so a bad `INSTANCE_ID` or domain fails before you run anything\n  on the server.\n- **Secrets never overwritten.** `provision-instance.sh` refuses to replace an existing\n  `.env.runtime` or Postgres password. Regenerating the password after the database\n  volume exists would lock the app out of its own database.\n- **Host key confirmed.** `configure-github-environment.sh` shows the host key\n  fingerprint and asks you to confirm it before trusting it.\n- **Key install fixed.** `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` installs the deploy key directly. This\n  replaces the `ssh-copy-id` step, which cannot work because the deploy account has a\n  locked password.\n- **Default deploy user changed.** `setup-server.sh` now defaults `APP_USER` to\n  `deploy` (it was `creame`). Pass `APP_USER` explicitly if you relied on the old\n  default.\n\n## What was tested\n\n- **Provisioning:** `provision-instance.sh` ran into a scratch directory.\n  - It created the files with mode 600.\n  - A second run left them untouched.\n  - It rejected a bad instance id and a `https://` domain.\n  - The Cloudinary variant warned about missing credentials.\n  - `EXTRA_ENV_FILE` was appended.\n- **Nginx and GitHub:** `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run` renders the vhost, and\n  `configure-github-environment.sh --dry-run` printed the right `gh` calls.\n- **A bug the tests caught:** an apostrophe broke the closing summary of\n  `provision-instance.sh`. It is fixed.\n\n## Not verified\n\n- **Real server:** nothing has run on an actual server. The `apt` installs, the certbot\n  webroot flow and the include swap in phase H follow the setup done by hand, but they\n  are untested as scripts.\n- **GitHub:** the `gh` writes (creating the Environment, setting variables and secrets)\n  have only been dry-run.\n- **Shellcheck:** not installed, so only `bash -n` was run.\n\nOn the next server, run `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run` first. It does not touch the\nlive `san-marina` instance.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1543,"cache_read_input_tokens":209078,"output_tokens":2059,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":235},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1543,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2059,"cache_read_input_tokens":209078,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1543,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1543},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01VAFXDZkTSVyDSUV8ev3wNu":{"file_path":"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell/docs/deployment/new-server-flow.md","content":"# New-server deployment flow: summary\n\nThe full runbook is [DEPLOYMENT.md](../../DEPLOYMENT.md). phase F uploads it to GitHub.\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nrequire_vars INSTANCE_ID PUBLIC_DOMAIN DEPLOY_HOST DEPLOY_USER GITHUB_REPO GHCR_USERNAME SSH_KEY_FILE\nderive_defaults''',1)\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\n\nd=open('DEPLOYMENT.md').read()\nold=d[d.index(\"### Phase B\"):d.index(\"### Phase C\")]\nnew='''### Phase B — Deploy key (laptop)\n\n```sh\nscripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/<id>.env --key-only\n```\n\nThis creates `$SSH_KEY_FILE` (ed25519, no passphrase — `webfactory/ssh-agent`\ncannot use passphrase-protected keys), never overwrites an existing one, and prints\nits **public** half: one line starting `ssh-ed25519 AAAA…`. Do not reuse your\npersonal key.\n\n**What to do with the output:** copy that whole line. You paste it into phase C as\n`SSH_PUBLIC_KEY='…'`, which authorises the key on the server. Keep the private file\non your machine; phase F uploads it to GitHub for you. Nothing else is needed, and\nnothing has been sent to the server or GitHub yet.\n\n'''\nd=d.replace(old,new,1)\nd=d.replace(\"`--generate-key --dry-run`\",\"`--key-only`\")\nopen('DEPLOYMENT.md','w').write(d)\nEOF\nbash -n scripts/configure-github-environment.sh && npx prettier --write DEPLOYMENT.md >/dev/null\nS=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-paullaster-Documents-projects-bigbro-qsell/166f5a26-a325-49b5-bd9f-cdd3ea150cc4/scratchpad\nprintf 'INSTANCE_ID=kt\\nSSH_KEY_FILE=%s/kt_key\\n' $S > $S/kt.env\nscripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config $S/kt.env --key-only | tail -8; echo ---rerun; scripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config $S/kt.env --key-only | head -1; rm -f $S/kt_key* $S/kt.env\ngrep -n \"generate-key\" DEPLOYMENT.md docs/deployment/new-server-flow.md"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":192497,"cache_read_input_tokens":23422,"output_tokens":2307,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":567},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":192497,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2307,"cache_read_input_tokens":23422,"cache_creation_input_tokens":192497,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":192497},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":{"cache_miss_reason":{"type":"previous_message_not_found"}},"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01FqYwcDKsP4v6FmTpH78y63":{"command":"cd /home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell && python3 - <<'EOF'\np='scripts/configure-github-environment.sh'\ns=open(p).read()\ns=s.replace(\"\"\"#   scripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/new-shop.env [--generate-key] [--yes] [--dry-run]\n\"\"\",\"\"\"#   scripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/new-shop.env --key-only\n#   scripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/new-shop.env [--yes] [--dry-run]\n#\n# --key-only      create the deploy key (if missing), print its PUBLIC half, and stop.\n#                 Needs no network access and changes nothing on GitHub.\n# --generate-key  like above, but then continue with the GitHub configuration.\n\"\"\",1)\ns=s.replace(\"GENERATE_KEY=0; What you do with it depends on which command you ran.\n\n**If you ran it as the docs said, with `--dry-run`:** the script never created a key. Nothing useful came out, so ignore that output. The docs were wrong, and I've fixed them.\n\n**What to run instead (the docs now say this):**\n```sh\nscripts/configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/<id>.env --key-only\n```\nIt creates the key at `SSH_KEY_FILE`, never overwrites an existing one, and prints a single line like:\n```\nssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nz…  qsell-actions-<id>\n```\n\n**What to do with that line:**\n1. Copy the whole line.\n2. In phase C, on the server, pass it as `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY='ssh-ed25519 AAAA… qsell-actions-<id>'` to `setup-server.sh`. That authorises the key for the deploy user. You can instead append the line to `~<deploy user>/.ssh/authorized_keys`.\n3. Keep the private file (`SSH_KEY_FILE`) on your own machine. Phase F uploads it to GitHub as the `DEPLOY_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` secret.\n\nThe key-only run sends nothing to the server or GitHub. I tested it locally: it created a key, printed the public line, and a second run left the key alone.\n\n**Your `noels-deliveries` deploy:** I haven't started it. I only read the Environment's settings, and I won't touch the server until you tell me to go ahead. Two things from that read:\n\n- **Tokens in the open.** `GHCR_READ_TOKEN` and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` are stored as plain Environment variables, not secrets, so their values were readable and printed in my output. Treat both tokens as exposed: revoke and reissue them, and store them as secrets. The real `GHCR_READ_TOKEN` secret is separate and already exists.\n- **Your server password** is also in this chat. Change it once we're done, or switch the `apps` user to key-only login. I haven't saved it anywhere.\n\nTwo caveats before I can use the server:\n\n- **Stale values.** The Environment's `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS` and `DEPLOY_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets are the dummy ones. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.\n- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.\n- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.\n- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.\n- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even \"change it\" or \"add a tab\". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.\n- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.\n- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.\n- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.\n- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like \"the xlsx in my downloads\") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.\n\n<total_tokens>15000000 tokens left</total_tokens>"}]}}

{"parentUuid":"f077abb4-7012-4091-82f9-ace148135d45","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7Dj8k1bt3Xukvk9DGda","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Phase D runs on the server as `apps`, not root and not with `sudo`. SSH in with your key:**\n```sh\nssh -i ~/.ssh/<your SSH_KEY_FILE> -o IdentitiesOnly=yes apps@13.140.158.165\n```\n\n**2. Create the config file on the server.** Change `ADMIN_EMAIL` to your real email. The other values already match what's in your GitHub Environment, and the defaults give the same path, project name and port:\n```sh\ncat > /tmp/noels-deliveries.env <<'EOF'\nINSTANCE_ID=noels-deliveries\nPUBLIC_DOMAIN=noelsdeliveries.com\nADMIN_EMAIL=you@example.com\nCERT_EMAIL=you@example.com\nMEDIA_DRIVER=local\nEOF\n```\n`MEDIA_DRIVER=local` stores images on the server's disk. Use `cloudinary` instead only if you already have Cloudinary credentials to add afterwards.\n\n**3. Run the script:**\n```sh\ncd /tmp\n./scripts/provision-instance.sh --config /tmp/noels-deliveries.env\n```\nIt asks for an initial admin password (16 or more characters, typed hidden, twice). If you press Enter on the first prompt, it generates one and shows it once on screen. Save that password right away in a password manager.\n\n**4. Check the result:**\n```sh\nls -la /opt/qsell/instances/noels-deliveries /opt/qsell/instances/noels-deliveries/secrets\n```\nYou should see `.env.runtime` and `secrets/postgres_password`, both mode `-rw-------` and owned by `apps`. The script's last lines also print the GitHub variables it expects.\n\n- **Don't re-run it expecting new secrets.** A second run leaves existing files untouched, on purpose.\n- **Back up two values.** `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `PAYMENT_DATA_KEY` in `.env.runtime` are the app's encryption keys, and losing them makes encrypted data unreadable. Copy them somewhere safe: `grep -E '^(DATA|PAYMENT_DATA)_ENCRYPTION_KEY|^PAYMENT_DATA_KEY' /opt/qsell/instances/noels-deliveries/.env.runtime`.\n\nTell me if the script prints any error. Next is phase E, the Nginx and TLS step. {"parentUuid":"1be8ffcf-6ca1-486e-88cd-e17fd00e4ff0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7Esns4Nw8etWyQ5dURg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Phase D worked. `.env.runtime` and the Postgres password now exist at `/opt/qsell/instances/noels-deliveries`, both mode 600. Before phase E, there are two jobs.\n\n**1. Add the Cloudinary credentials.** The deploy refuses to run without them, as the warning said. Edit the file on the server:\n```sh\nnano /opt/qsell/instances/noels-deliveries/.env.runtime\n```\nFind the `# TODO` line near the bottom and add one of these (get the values from the Cloudinary console):\n```\nCLOUDINARY_URL=cloudinary://API_KEY:API_SECRET@CLOUD_NAME\n```\nor the three separate lines `CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME=`, `CLOUDINARY_API_KEY=` and `CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET=`. Use nano rather than `echo`, so the secret doesn't end up in your shell history. Then confirm the keys are present without printing their values:\n```sh\ngrep -E '^(MEDIA_DRIVER|CLOUDINARY_)' /opt/qsell/instances/noels-deliveries/.env.runtime | sed 's/=.*/=…/'\n```\nIf you don't have Cloudinary credentials yet, set `MEDIA_DRIVER=local` in that file instead, and switch later.\n\n**2. Back up the encryption keys** (and the admin password if you let it generate one):\n```sh\ngrep -E '^(DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY|PAYMENT_DATA_KEY)=' /opt/qsell/instances/noels-deliveries/.env.runtime\n```\nSave both lines in a password manager. Losing them makes encrypted data unreadable.\n\n**Check before phase E** (Nginx and TLS). Certbot will fail if either of these is wrong:\n- **DNS.** `shop.noelsdeliveries.com` must resolve to `13.140.158.165`. Check with `dig +short shop.noelsdeliveries.com`. {"parentUuid":"f688a12e-dc1f-4f3c-a7c1-765191acd2cd","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7F9GcLDEzJUe7htJ2ST","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Run it on the server from `/tmp`:\n\n```sh\ncd /tmp\nsudo ./scripts/setup-nginx-site.sh --config /tmp/noels-deliveries.env\n```\n\nFirst, check that DNS is ready, since the certificate request fails otherwise:\n```sh\ndig +short shop.noelsdeliveries.com    # must print 13.140.158.165\n```\nIf `dig` is missing, run `getent hosts shop.noelsdeliveries.com`. If it prints nothing or a different IP, fix the DNS record first. With Cloudflare, the record must be **DNS only** (grey cloud) until the certificate is issued.\n\nWhat the script does:\n1. Installs Nginx and certbot.\n2. Checks that the domain resolves, and stops with a clear message if it doesn't.\n3. Requests the certificate for `shop.noelsdeliveries.com`, using `ops` contact email `paullasterokoth98@gmail.com`.\n4. Writes `/etc/nginx/sites-available/noels-deliveries` and enables it. It removes the default site.\n5. Runs `nginx -t` and reloads Nginx.\n\nIt finishes with `Done. shop.noelsdeliveries.com answers 503 until the first deploy`. A 503 at this stage is correct.\n\nCheck it after it finishes:\n```sh\ncurl -sI https://shop.noelsdeliveries.com | head -1    # HTTP/2 503\n```\n\nIf certbot fails, the usual causes are that port 80 is blocked by your provider's firewall, DNS hasn't spread yet, or the Cloudflare proxy is on. Paste the last lines of the error and I'll sort it out.\n\nBefore the deploy in phase G, do two things on your laptop. Run phase F (`configure-github-environment.sh --config deploy/instances/noels-deliveries.env`). It replaces the dummy Environment values and the host key secret. And add `shop.noelsdeliveries.com` to `SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, then publish a new release build."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":43,"cache_read_input_tokens":231897,"output_tokens":684,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":43,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":684,"cache_read_input_tokens":231897,"cache_creation_input_tokens":43,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":43},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"2af1f463-d69d-4eba-891e-ba6121faf61d","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011Cg7F9FtfV55AV9GpPh3sa","requestRef":"db1dbc15-ad88-4e97-8cb8-835f38c089f7","requestedModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"abfbcb8a-cfdf-4581-9c9d-0ec70c89a67c","timestamp":"2026-10-17T05:19:00.006Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"166f5a26-a325-49b5-bd9f-cdd3ea150cc4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell","sessionId":"166f5a26-a325-49b5-bd9f-cdd3ea150cc4","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"feat/finance-f4"}

This page summarises the\nconfig-file-driven flow and what the scripts do.\n\n## How it works\n\nYou fill in one file per server, `deploy/instances/<id>.env`, and every script reads\nit. The template is `deploy/instance.env.example`; real copies are git-ignored.\n\n- A value passed as an environment variable overrides the file.\n- Defaults are derived from `INSTANCE_ID`:\n  - directory: `$APP_DIR/instances/<id>` (`APP_DIR` defaults to `/opt/qsell`)\n  - Compose project name: `qsell-<id>`\n  - loopback port: `8080`\n- There are no hardcoded users, IPs or domains.\n\n| Step                                                      | Script                                                               | Where it runs              |\n| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |\n| Create the deploy key                                     | `configure-github-environment.sh --key-only`                         | your laptop                |\n| Bootstrap the host                                        | `setup-server.sh` (takes `APP_USER`, `APP_DIR` and `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`) | server, as root            |\n| Create the instance directory, secrets and `.env.runtime` | `provision-instance.sh`                                              | server, as the deploy user |\n| Nginx, certificate and vhost                              | `setup-nginx-site.sh`                                                | server, as root            |\n| Create the GitHub Environment (7 variables, 3 secrets)    | `configure-github-environment.sh`                                    | your laptop                |\n| Deploy                                                    | the \"Deploy release to instance\" workflow (the SHA is optional)      | GitHub                     |\n| Switch the site on                                        | `setup-nginx-site.sh --no-cert` (re-run after the first deploy)      | server, as root            |\n\n## What `DEPLOYMENT.md` covers\n\n- An architecture diagram.\n- The full parameter table: what each value means, its rules, its default, and where\n  it ends up in GitHub.\n- One-time repository setup.\n- Phases A to I for a new server, with a go-live checklist.\n- The release flow, rollback behaviour and operations (logs, backups, adding a domain,\n  decommissioning).\n- A troubleshooting table covering the errors hit while setting up `san-marina`:\n  - the missing `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` variable\n  - the underscore in the instance id\n  - the `MEDIA_DRIVER` typo\n  - the locked-account `ssh-copy-id` problem\n  - the unset `RELEASE_SHA`\n  - the missing Nginx include\n\n## Mistakes the scripts now prevent\n\n- **Config checked before CI.** They validate your values with the same rules the\n  deploy workflow uses, so a bad `INSTANCE_ID` or domain fails before you run anything\n  on the server.\n- **Secrets never overwritten.** `provision-instance.sh` refuses to replace an existing\n  `.env.runtime` or Postgres password. Regenerating the password after the database\n  volume exists would lock the app out of its own database.\n- **Host key confirmed.** `configure-github-environment.sh` shows the host key\n  fingerprint and asks you to confirm it before trusting it.\n- **Key install fixed.** `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` installs the deploy key directly. This\n  replaces the `ssh-copy-id` step, which cannot work because the deploy account has a\n  locked password.\n- **Default deploy user changed.** `setup-server.sh` now defaults `APP_USER` to\n  `deploy` (it was `creame`). Pass `APP_USER` explicitly if you relied on the old\n  default.\n\n## What was tested\n\n- **Provisioning:** `provision-instance.sh` ran into a scratch directory.\n  - It created the files with mode 600.\n  - A second run left them untouched.\n  - It rejected a bad instance id and a `https://` domain.\n  - The Cloudinary variant warned about missing credentials.\n  - `EXTRA_ENV_FILE` was appended.\n- **Nginx and GitHub:** `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run` renders the vhost, and\n  `configure-github-environment.sh --dry-run` printed the right `gh` calls.\n- **A bug the tests caught:** an apostrophe broke the closing summary of\n  `provision-instance.sh`. It is fixed.\n\n## Not verified\n\n- **Real server:** nothing has run on an actual server. The `apt` installs, the certbot\n  webroot flow and the include swap in phase H follow the setup done by hand, but they\n  are untested as scripts.\n- **GitHub:** the `gh` writes (creating the Environment, setting variables and secrets)\n  have only been dry-run.\n- **Shellcheck:** not installed, so only `bash -n` was run.\n\nOn the next server, run `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run` first. `ssh-copy-id` problem\n42\t  - the unset `RELEASE_SHA`\n43\t  - the missing Nginx include\n44\t\n45\t## Mistakes the scripts now prevent\n46\t\n47\t- **Config checked before CI.** They validate your values with the same rules the\n48\t  deploy workflow uses, so a bad `INSTANCE_ID` or domain fails before you run anything\n49\t  on the server.\n50\t- **Secrets never overwritten.** `provision-instance.sh` refuses to replace an existing\n51\t  `.env.runtime` or Postgres password. Regenerating the password after the database\n52\t  volume exists would lock the app out of its own database.\n53\t- **Host key confirmed.** `configure-github-environment.sh` shows the host key\n54\t  fingerprint and asks you to confirm it before trusting it.\n55\t- **Key install fixed.** `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` installs the deploy key directly. This\n56\t  replaces the `ssh-copy-id` step, which cannot work because the deploy account has a\n57\t  locked password.\n58\t- **Default deploy user changed.** `setup-server.sh` now defaults `APP_USER` to\n59\t  `deploy` (it was `creame`). Pass `APP_USER` explicitly if you relied on the old\n60\t  default.\n61\t\n62\t## What was tested\n63\t\n64\t- **Provisioning:** `provision-instance.sh` ran into a scratch directory.\n65\t  - It created the files with mode 600.\n66\t  - A second run left them untouched.\n67\t  - It rejected a bad instance id and a `https://` domain.\n68\t  - The Cloudinary variant warned about missing credentials.\n69\t  - `EXTRA_ENV_FILE` was appended.\n70\t- **Nginx and GitHub:** `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run` renders the vhost, and\n71\t  `configure-github-environment.sh --dry-run` printed the right `gh` calls.\n72\t- **A bug the tests caught:** an apostrophe broke the closing summary of\n73\t  `provision-instance.sh`. It is fixed.\n74\t\n75\t## Not verified\n76\t\n77\t- **Real server:** nothing has run on an actual server. The `apt` installs, the certbot\n78\t  webroot flow and the include swap in phase H follow the setup done by hand, but they\n79\t  are untested as scripts.\n80\t- **GitHub:** the `gh` writes (creating the Environment, setting variables and secrets)\n81\t  have only been dry-run.\n82\t- **Shellcheck:** not installed, so only `bash -n` was run.\n83\t\n84\tOn the next server, run `setup-nginx-site.sh --dry-run` first. It does not touch the\n85\tlive `san-marina` instance.\n86\t\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"system","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell","sessionId":"166f5a26-a325-49b5-bd9f-cdd3ea150cc4","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"feat/finance-f4","slug":"fizzy-weaving-deer"}

5432:5432\n        options: >-\n          --health-cmd=\"pg_isready -U qsell -d qsell\"\n          --health-interval=5s\n          --health-timeout=3s\n          --health-retries=12\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4\n        with:\n          version: 12.6.0\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4\n        with:\n          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}\n          cache: pnpm\n      - name: Install locked dependencies\n        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n      - name: Apply database migrations\n        run: pnpm db:migrate\n        env:\n          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://qsell:ci-only-password@localhost:5432/qsell\n      - name: Typecheck\n        run: pnpm typecheck\n      - name: Run unit, integration and API tests\n        # Integration tests run against the migrated database above (built from the\n        # migration SQL, so the hand-added append-only triggers are exercised).\n        # Lint is not gated yet: it crashes under ESLint 10 and has pre-existing violations.\n        run: pnpm test\n        env:\n          TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://qsell:ci-only-password@localhost:5432/qsell\n          AUTH_SECRET: ci-only-auth-secret-not-for-deployment\n      - name: Verify media storage adapters\n        # Runs the Cloudinary adapter against a local fake: retries, timeouts, signed private\n        # links and the \"private upload must not land public\" safety check. No credentials needed.\n        run: pnpm media:verify\n      - name: Production build\n        run: pnpm build\n        env:\n          NODE_ENV: production\n          AUTH_SECRET: ci-only-auth-secret-not-for-deployment\n          NEXTAUTH_URL: http://localhost:3069\n          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://qsell:ci-only-password@localhost:5432/qsell\n\n  e2e:\n    name: End-to-end tests\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    timeout-minutes: 40\n    services:\n      postgres:\n        image: postgres:18-alpine\n        env:\n          POSTGRES_DB: qsell_e2e\n          POSTGRES_USER: qsell\n          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ci-only-password\n        ports:\n          - 5432:5432\n        options: >-\n          --health-cmd=\"pg_isready -U qsell -d qsell_e2e\"\n          --health-interval=5s\n          --health-timeout=3s\n          --health-retries=12\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4\n        with:\n          version: 12.6.0\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4\n        with:\n          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}\n          cache: pnpm\n      - name: Install locked dependencies\n        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n      - name: Install Chrome and the tools the run uses\n        # Chrome drives the tests; psmisc provides fuser, which stops the test server afterwards.\n        run: |\n          sudo apt-get update\n          sudo apt-get install -y psmisc\n          pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chrome\n      - name: Run end-to-end tests (desktop and phone width)\n        # The run migrates, seeds and logs in on its own database and port; see e2e/README.md.\n        run: pnpm test:e2e\n        env:\n          E2E_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://qsell:ci-only-password@localhost:5432/qsell_e2e\n          AUTH_SECRET: ci-only-auth-secret-not-for-deployment\n          JWT_SECRET: ci-only-jwt-secret-not-for-deployment\n          DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ci-only-data-encryption-key-not-for-deployment\n          CI: 'true'\n      - name: Keep the report when a test fails\n        if: failure()\n        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4\n        with:\n          name: e2e-results\n          path: test-results\n          retention-days: 7\n\n  publish:\n    name: Build and publish release images\n    needs: [validate, e2e]\n    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/release'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3\n      - uses: docker/login-action@v3\n        with:\n          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}\n          username: ${{ github.actor }}\n          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}\n\n      - name: Build and publish web image\n        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6\n        with:\n          context: .\n          target: runner\n          push: true\n          platforms: linux/amd64\n          tags: ${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:sha-${{ github.sha }}\n          cache-from: type=gha,scope=web\n          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=web\n          build-args: |\n            DEPLOYMENT_VERSION=${{ github.sha }}\n            NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=${{ vars.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN }}\n            SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${{ vars.SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS || 'omnicommerce.brainsporellc.com' }}\n          secrets: |\n            sentry_auth_token=${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}\n\n      - name: Build and publish worker image\n        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6\n        with:\n          context: .\n          target: worker\n          push: true\n          platforms: linux/amd64\n          tags: ${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:worker-${{ github.sha }}\n          cache-from: type=gha,scope=worker\n          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=worker\n\n      - {"parentUuid":"626dac05-e88d-43a7-894c-842f73a3074b","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"file","filename":"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell/Dockerfile","content":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell/Dockerfile","content":"# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7\n\nARG NODE_VERSION=24\nFROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine AS base\nWORKDIR /app\nENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \\\n    PNPM_HOME=/pnpm \\\n    COREPACK_HOME=/pnpm/corepack \\\n    PATH=/pnpm:$PATH\nRUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@12.6.0 --activate\n\n# Install the exact pnpm version and dependency graph declared by the manifest\n# and lockfile. A missing lockfile fails the image build instead of resolving\n# newer dependency versions implicitly.\nFROM base AS dependencies\nCOPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml ./\nRUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm-store,target=/pnpm/store \\\n    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n\n# Local development target. Compose bind-mounts the source tree.\nFROM dependencies AS development\nENV NODE_ENV=development PORT=3069 HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0\nEXPOSE 3069\nCMD [\"pnpm\", \"dev\", \"--hostname\", \"0.0.0.0\", \"--port\", \"3069\"]\n\n# Compile the web application once. Standalone output contains its traced\n# production runtime dependencies and does not need a second dependency install.\nFROM dependencies AS builder\nCOPY . .\nARG DEPLOYMENT_VERSION=local\nARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN\nARG SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=omnicommerce.brainsporellc.com\n# src/auth.ts validates AUTH_SECRET during module initialization at build time.\n# This is a disposable build-only value; the runtime secret comes from .env.runtime.\nENV NODE_ENV=production \\\n    AUTH_SECRET=build-only-not-a-runtime-secret \\\n    DEPLOYMENT_VERSION=${DEPLOYMENT_VERSION} \\\n    NEXT_PUBLIC_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION=${DEPLOYMENT_VERSION} \\\n    NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=${NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN} \\\n    SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${SERVER_ACTION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS}\nRUN --mount=type=secret,id=sentry_auth_token,target=/run/secrets/sentry-auth-token,required=false \\\n    SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=\"$(cat /run/secrets/sentry-auth-token 2>/dev/null || true)\" pnpm build\n\nFROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine AS runtime-base\nWORKDIR /app\nENV NODE_ENV=production \\\n    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \\\n    PORT=3069 \\\n    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 \\\n    HOME=/home/nextjs \\\n    PNPM_HOME=/pnpm \\\n    COREPACK_HOME=/pnpm/corepack \\\n    PATH=/pnpm:$PATH \\\n    # Media storage works out of the box: uploads go to this directory, which the production\n    # Compose file mounts as a persistent volume on BOTH the app and the worker. A value in\n    # .env.runtime (e.g. MEDIA_DRIVER=cloudinary) overrides these defaults.\n    MEDIA_DRIVER=local \\\n    MEDIA_LOCAL_DIR=/app/storage/media\n# /app/storage/media is created here, owned by the app user, so a fresh named volume mounted\n# on it inherits that ownership and the unprivileged app can write to it.\nRUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nextjs \\\n && adduser --system --uid 1001 --ingroup nextjs nextjs \\\n && mkdir -p /home/nextjs/.cache /app/storage/media \\\n && corepack enable \\\n && corepack prepare pnpm@12.6.0 --activate \\\n && chown -R nextjs:nextjs /pnpm \\\n && chown -R nextjs:nextjs /home/nextjs /app\n\n# pnpm 12 resolves its pinned standalone executable from the project lockfile.\n# Warm that cache during image build so production worker/migration containers\n# never need registry/DNS access at startup. HOME is identical at runtime.\nCOPY --from=dependencies --chown=nextjs:nextjs /app/package.json /app/pnpm-lock.yaml /app/pnpm-workspace.yaml ./\nUSER nextjs\nRUN pnpm --version\nUSER root\n\nFROM runtime-base AS runner\nCOPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nextjs /app/.next/standalone ./\nCOPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nextjs /app/.next/static ./.next/static\nCOPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nextjs /app/public ./public\nRUN mkdir -p .next/cache && chown -R nextjs:nextjs .next\nUSER nextjs\nEXPOSE 3069\nHEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=30s --retries=3 \\\n  CMD [\"node\", \"-e\", \"fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3069/api/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))\"]\nCMD [\"node\", \"server.js\"]\n\n# Background worker has a distinct runtime: Graphile Worker runs TypeScript\n# task handlers via tsx and shares the same pinned dependency lockfile.\nFROM runtime-base AS worker\nCOPY --from=dependencies --chown=nextjs:nextjs /app/node_modules ./node_modules\nCOPY --chown=nextjs:nextjs package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml tsconfig.json ./\nCOPY --chown=nextjs:nextjs src ./src\n# Operational scripts (media provider check, manual sweep) run from this image so they\n# see the same dependencies, environment and network access as the real worker.\nCOPY --chown=nextjs:nextjs scripts ./scripts\nUSER nextjs\nCMD [\"pnpm\", \"worker\"]\n\n# One-shot Drizzle migration image. Deploy runs this image before replacing app\n# containers, so schema changes are applied using the same source revision.\nFROM runtime-base AS migrator\nCOPY --from=dependencies --chown=nextjs:nextjs /app/node_modules ./node_modules\nCOPY --chown=nextjs:nextjs package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml tsconfig.json drizzle.config.ts ./\nCOPY --chown=nextjs:nextjs drizzle ./drizzle\nCOPY --chown=nextjs:nextjs src ./src\nUSER nextjs\nCMD [\"pnpm\", \"db:migrate\"]\n","numLines":109,"startLine":1,"totalLines":109}},"displayPath":"Dockerfile"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"55e76f69-160a-4ba9-84fb-3af2de598173","timestamp":"2026-10-17T06:17:33.222Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nCalled the Read tool with the following input: {\"file_path\":\"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell/Dockerfile\"}\n</system-reminder>"},{"content":"<system-reminder>\nResult of calling the Read tool:\n1\t# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7\n2\t\n3\tARG NODE_VERSION=24\n4\tFROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine AS base\n5\tWORKDIR /app\n6\tENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \\\n7\t    PNPM_HOME=/pnpm \\\n8\t    COREPACK_HOME=/pnpm/corepack \\\n9\t    PATH=/pnpm:$PATH\n10\tRUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@12.6.0 --activate\n11\t\n12\t# Install the exact pnpm version and dependency graph declared by the manifest\n13\t# and lockfile. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)\n- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: \"medium\" for moderate exploration, \"very thorough\" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: *)\n- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. {"parentUuid":"5771ceb4-9afd-4865-848c-b2f64c6af4d0","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["claude.ai Claude Docs"],"addedBlocks":["## claude.ai Claude Docs\nClaude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {\"kind\":\"project\",\"create\":{\"name\":\"<title>\",\"doc\":{\"blocks\":{\"asof\":{\"type\":\"date\",\"value\":\"<today>\"},\"me\":{\"type\":\"mention\",\"user\":\"me\"},\"s1\":{\"type\":\"pending\",\"intent\":\"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to\"},\"s2\":{…}},\"markdown\":\"# <title>\\n\\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\\n\\n<?claude block s1?>\\n\\n<?claude block s2?>\"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: \"<root id>\"`."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"38d45ee6-19b5-459c-b48c-1dee9cf80bb7","timestamp":"2026-10-17T06:17:33.235Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\n# MCP Server Instructions\n\nThe following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:\n\n## claude.ai Claude Docs\nClaude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. Every agent and contributor must follow them."},{"path":"/home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell/docs/PROJECT_RULES.md","type":"Project","content":"# qsell project rules\n\nThese rules are **permanent and non-negotiable** for every person and every AI agent that works on this project. Read them before changing anything. If existing code breaks a rule, say so and fix it properly; never copy the pattern.\n\n## 1. Pinned stack\n\n| Package | Version |\n|---|---|\n| `next` | 16.4.0 |\n| `react`, `react-dom` | 19.3.0 |\n| `eslint` | 10.12.0 |\n| `typescript` | ~7.0.2 (via the `@typescript/native` alias; `typescript` is aliased to 6.x for tooling) |\n| package manager | pnpm 12.6.0, Node 24 |\n\nNever downgrade these to suit another package: adapt the other package or the config. Check a new dependency's peer ranges first. Next.js here is **not the Next.js you may remember**: read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing Next code (`params` and `searchParams` are Promises). Use the standard Next folder structure. TypeScript 7: no `baseUrl`, `types` defaults to `[]`, no programmatic API.\n\n## 2. Quality bar (every change, no trade-offs)\n\n1. **UX**: clear loading, empty, error and success states; confirm before destructive actions (inline confirm, never `window.confirm`); nothing lost silently; plain-language messages.\n2. **Security**: hard to break into and hard to tamper with. Every action checks its permission **on the server**; every query is company-scoped; all input is validated on the server; no client-supplied ids, prices or flags are trusted; no injection, XSS, CSRF or IDOR; secrets and internal errors never reach the screen; credentials are stored sealed and never printed or logged.\n3. **Responsive**: 390px phones to desktop, no horizontal scrolling (page or inner boxes), cards on phones and tables from `md`, touch targets of 40px or more.\n4. **Scalable**: no N+1 queries (batch with `inArray`), long lists are paged on the server (keyset), new query paths get indexes, nothing grows per row at render or save.\n5. **Reliable**: multi-row writes in transactions, failures returned as data (server-action errors are masked in production), consistent saves.\n6. **Maintainable**: small focused modules, pure logic apart from UI, match the surrounding code, comments only for the non-obvious why.\n7. **Reusable**: extend existing components instead of copying (`ChoicePicker`, `LookupAutocomplete`, `usePagedList`, `InlineConfirm`, `screen-kit`, `RouteModal`).\n8. **Accessible**: labelled controls, dialog roles with focus management and Escape, `role=\"alert\"` / `aria-live`, keyboard operable, WCAG AA contrast.\n9. **SEO**: public pages have metadata, semantic headings and landmarks; admin stays noindex.\n\n## 3. Architecture\n\n- **Server components by default.** A client component only where a person interacts or a browser API is needed; split the interactive part into its own small client island.\n- **No logic in components** (server components included): no business rules, validation, database access or external connections inside a component. Components render and call **server actions**; everything else lives on the server.\n- **Client data is never trusted.** The browser validates for convenience; the server validates for real and never relies on the browser.\n- **Purity.** Every component and every function is pure: same inputs, same output, no side effects or reads of changing values (time, randomness, refs, globals) during render. Pass the clock, ids and data in as parameters. Impure edges (database, network, session) stay thin, named and out of components.\n- **Server actions return results as data** (`{ ok, data } | { ok: false, error }`) through the shared runners (`runSetting`, finance `run`, ...), each with one explicit permission; the company and the person are set on the server.\n\n## 4. Selection inputs: Autocomplete, never `<select>`\n\nAny input that picks from options uses the shared **ChoicePicker / LookupAutocomplete**. Native `<select>` is never used.\n\n- It never holds the whole list: it loads **one page at a time (default 20)**, **only when focused**, and searches **on the server** (debounced, stale answers ignored) in a server action over configured columns.\n- Lists are registered as lookup sources in `src/server/domains/lookups/sources.ts` (fixed lists with `staticSource`, tables with `tableSource`), each behind a permission.\n- Offer **create new** and **view all** as routes using **intercepting routes + parallel-route slots** (`@create`, `@modal`): a modal on soft navigation, a full page on a direct URL.\n\n## 5. Non-blocking, parallel loading\n\nEvery `page.tsx` is a server component. **Do not `await` unless something must be decided before the screen shows** (a security or validation decision). Otherwise pass the **un-awaited promise** to a client component that reads it with `use()` inside `<Suspense>` (`SettingsFrame` / `FinancePage` do this). Independent parts of a screen load independently and in parallel.\n\nA record that does not exist shows the not-found page through `MissingAs404` (malformed ids count as missing). Lists are paged with keyset cursors (`settings/paging.ts`; timestamp cursors keep microseconds).\n\n## 6. Tests: the full pyramid for every feature\n\nEvery feature ships with **unit, integration, API and e2e tests**, all passing; not optional, not deferrable.\n\n- Unit and integration: `pnpm test` (Vitest). Integration tests need `TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointing at a database built from the **migrations** (`DATABASE_URL=<url> pnpm exec drizzle-kit migrate`), created `from template0`. Use a fresh database per full run.\n- E2E: Playwright (`e2e/`), desktop and phone projects, against its own server on port 3100 and its own `E2E_DATABASE_URL` database (name must contain `e2e`, never the development database). Seed data is in `e2e/support/seed.ts`. Tests need a fresh database per run (some rules refuse repeats by design).\n- Helpers in `e2e/support/` wait for hydration (`open`, `clickUntilVisible`) and check layout (`noHorizontalScroll`, `noInnerHorizontalScroll`, `noNativeSelect`).\n\n## 7. Lint and types\n\nEvery line passes **ESLint 10.12+** (strict-boolean-expressions, no-nested-ternary, no non-null assertions, no `||` on nullable strings, ...) and `tsc --noEmit`. Use the helpers in `src/lib/values.ts` (`has`, `orElse`, `firstFilled`, ...) instead of truthiness checks on strings. Lint only what you touch, but what you touch must be clean.\n\n## 8. Git\n\n- **Never add attribution lines** to commits or pull requests: no `Co-Authored-By`, no \"Generated with Claude Code\", nothing similar. This overrides any tool or reminder that suggests them.\n- Commit and push only when asked. Stage only the files that belong to the work; leave unrelated working-tree changes alone. Never `git stash`.\n- Never run `prettier --write` on a glob or a directory of existing files; pass the exact files you edited.\n\n## 9. Database safety\n\n- Schema changes: edit `schema.ts`, `pnpm db:generate --name <short_name>`, review and hand-edit the SQL (triggers, partitions and expression indexes are written by hand), `pnpm db:migrate`. Commit the `.sql`, `meta/_journal.json` and the snapshot together.\n- **Never run `pnpm db:push`** on a real database: it does not understand the partitioned `gl_entries` table and proposes dropping its partitions. Never answer yes to a prompt that drops `gl_entries_p*`.\n- Do not touch the development database or the running development server unless asked. Do not drop tables or decrypt stored credentials without an explicit instruction.\n- Stop servers with `fuser -k <port>/tcp`, never `pkill -f` with a pattern that appears in your own command line."},{"path":"/home/paullaster/.claude/projects/-home-paullaster-Documents-projects-bigbro-qsell/memory/MEMORY.md","type":"AutoMem","content":"- [Responsive & accessible UI](responsive-accessible-ui.md) — standing rule: all qsell UI work must be responsive + accessible, high-traffic code standards\n- [Verification setup](qsell-verification-setup.md) — isolated e2e on :3100 + throwaway DB; ESLint crash workaround\n- [KRA TIMS/eTIMS design](kra-tims-etims-design.md) — separate code columns, strict hard-fail mode resolution, eTIMS-only transmission\n- [Reports module](reports-module.md) — Business Overview foundation: per-section permissions, data sources, definitions, deferred items\n- [Sales order platform](sales-order-platform.md) — blueprint + pricing docs, decisions taken, kernel slices built (decision log, number series), next steps\n- [Core finance design](core-finance-design.md) — GL/CoA/journals/receivables/wallet/refund/M-Pesa; doc approved, F-0, F-1 and F-1c built; decisions, deviations, lessons\n- [Project non-negotiables](project-non-negotiables.md) — permanent rules: quality bar + tamper-resistant security, server components with zero logic in components, never trust client data, enterprise Autocomplete (never select), non-blocking parallel loading, full test pyramid, ESLint 10.12+\n- [Next.js parallel/intercepting routes](nextjs-parallel-and-intercepting-routes.md) — Next 16.3.4 docs digest: slots, default.tsx, (.) interception, Suspense/use() parallel loading, qsell's @modal/@create setup\n- [Next.js 16.4.0 default](nextjs-16-4-default-version.md) — default version + folder-structure rule; Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).\n\n## Picking delaySeconds\n\nThis session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)\n\nMatch the delay to what you're actually waiting for:\n\n- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:\n- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned\n- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task\n- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request\n- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked\n\nThe draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.\n\nWrite `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:\n- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.\n- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write \"User didn't comment; observed by the model.\" Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.\n- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.\n- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.\n\nConstraints:\n- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.\n- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.\n- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. \"hooks config\", \"/help\", \"file editing\") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.\n- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.\n- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.\n- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role (\"a teammate\", \"the PR reviewer\"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. Every agent and contributor must follow them.\n\nContents of /home/paullaster/Documents/projects/bigbro/qsell/docs/PROJECT_RULES.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# qsell project rules\n\nThese rules are **permanent and non-negotiable** for every person and every AI agent that works on this project. Read them before changing anything. If existing code breaks a rule, say so and fix it properly; never copy the pattern.\n\n## 1. Pinned stack\n\n| Package | Version |\n|---|---|\n| `next` | 16.4.0 |\n| `react`, `react-dom` | 19.3.0 |\n| `eslint` | 10.12.0 |\n| `typescript` | ~7.0.2 (via the `@typescript/native` alias; `typescript` is aliased to 6.x for tooling) |\n| package manager | pnpm 12.6.0, Node 24 |\n\nNever downgrade these to suit another package: adapt the other package or the config. Check a new dependency's peer ranges first. Next.js here is **not the Next.js you may remember**: read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing Next code (`params` and `searchParams` are Promises). Use the standard Next folder structure. TypeScript 7: no `baseUrl`, `types` defaults to `[]`, no programmatic API.\n\n## 2. Quality bar (every change, no trade-offs)\n\n1. **UX**: clear loading, empty, error and success states; confirm before destructive actions (inline confirm, never `window.confirm`); nothing lost silently; plain-language messages.\n2. **Security**: hard to break into and hard to tamper with. Every action checks its permission **on the server**; every query is company-scoped; all input is validated on the server; no client-supplied ids, prices or flags are trusted; no injection, XSS, CSRF or IDOR; secrets and internal errors never reach the screen; credentials are stored sealed and never printed or logged.\n3. **Responsive**: 390px phones to desktop, no horizontal scrolling (page or inner boxes), cards on phones and tables from `md`, touch targets of 40px or more.\n4. **Scalable**: no N+1 queries (batch with `inArray`), long lists are paged on the server (keyset), new query paths get indexes, nothing grows per row at render or save.\n5. **Reliable**: multi-row writes in transactions, failures returned as data (server-action errors are masked in production), consistent saves.\n6. **Maintainable**: small focused modules, pure logic apart from UI, match the surrounding code, comments only for the non-obvious why.\n7. **Reusable**: extend existing components instead of copying (`ChoicePicker`, `LookupAutocomplete`, `usePagedList`, `InlineConfirm`, `screen-kit`, `RouteModal`).\n8. **Accessible**: labelled controls, dialog roles with focus management and Escape, `role=\"alert\"` / `aria-live`, keyboard operable, WCAG AA contrast.\n9. **SEO**: public pages have metadata, semantic headings and landmarks; admin stays noindex.\n\n## 3. Architecture\n\n- **Server components by default.** A client component only where a person interacts or a browser API is needed; split the interactive part into its own small client island.\n- **No logic in components** (server components included): no business rules, validation, database access or external connections inside a component. Components render and call **server actions**; everything else lives on the server.\n- **Client data is never trusted.** The browser validates for convenience; the server validates for real and never relies on the browser.\n- **Purity.** Every component and every function is pure: same inputs, same output, no side effects or reads of changing values (time, randomness, refs, globals) during render. Pass the clock, ids and data in as parameters. Impure edges (database, network, session) stay thin, named and out of components.\n- **Server actions return results as data** (`{ ok, data } | { ok: false, error }`) through the shared runners (`runSetting`, finance `run`, ...), each with one explicit permission; the company and the person are set on the server.\n\n## 4. Selection inputs: Autocomplete, never `<select>`\n\nAny input that picks from options uses the shared **ChoicePicker / LookupAutocomplete**. Native `<select>` is never used.\n\n- It never holds the whole list: it loads **one page at a time (default 20)**, **only when focused**, and searches **on the server** (debounced, stale answers ignored) in a server action over configured columns.\n- Lists are registered as lookup sources in `src/server/domains/lookups/sources.ts` (fixed lists with `staticSource`, tables with `tableSource`), each behind a permission.\n- Offer **create new** and **view all** as routes using **intercepting routes + parallel-route slots** (`@create`, `@modal`): a modal on soft navigation, a full page on a direct URL.\n\n## 5. Non-blocking, parallel loading\n\nEvery `page.tsx` is a server component. **Do not `await` unless something must be decided before the screen shows** (a security or validation decision). Otherwise pass the **un-awaited promise** to a client component that reads it with `use()` inside `<Suspense>` (`SettingsFrame` / `FinancePage` do this). Independent parts of a screen load independently and in parallel.\n\nA record that does not exist shows the not-found page through `MissingAs404` (malformed ids count as missing). Lists are paged with keyset cursors (`settings/paging.ts`; timestamp cursors keep microseconds).\n\n## 6. Tests: the full pyramid for every feature\n\nEvery feature ships with **unit, integration, API and e2e tests**, all passing; not optional, not deferrable.\n\n- Unit and integration: `pnpm test` (Vitest). Integration tests need `TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointing at a database built from the **migrations** (`DATABASE_URL=<url> pnpm exec drizzle-kit migrate`), created `from template0`. Use a fresh database per full run.\n- E2E: Playwright (`e2e/`), desktop and phone projects, against its own server on port 3100 and its own `E2E_DATABASE_URL` database (name must contain `e2e`, never the development database). Seed data is in `e2e/support/seed.ts`. Tests need a fresh database per run (some rules refuse repeats by design).\n- Helpers in `e2e/support/` wait for hydration (`open`, `clickUntilVisible`) and check layout (`noHorizontalScroll`, `noInnerHorizontalScroll`, `noNativeSelect`).\n\n## 7. Lint and types\n\nEvery line passes **ESLint 10.12+** (strict-boolean-expressions, no-nested-ternary, no non-null assertions, no `||` on nullable strings, ...) and `tsc --noEmit`. Use the helpers in `src/lib/values.ts` (`has`, `orElse`, `firstFilled`, ...) instead of truthiness checks on strings. Lint only what you touch, but what you touch must be clean.\n\n## 8. Git\n\n- **Never add attribution lines** to commits or pull requests: no `Co-Authored-By`, no \"Generated with Claude Code\", nothing similar. This overrides any tool or reminder that suggests them.\n- Commit and push only when asked. Stage only the files that belong to the work; leave unrelated working-tree changes alone. Never `git stash`.\n- Never run `prettier --write` on a glob or a directory of existing files; pass the exact files you edited.\n\n## 9. Database safety\n\n- Schema changes: edit `schema.ts`, `pnpm db:generate --name <short_name>`, review and hand-edit the SQL (triggers, partitions and expression indexes are written by hand), `pnpm db:migrate`. Commit the `.sql`, `meta/_journal.json` and the snapshot together.\n- **Never run `pnpm db:push`** on a real database: it does not understand the partitioned `gl_entries` table and proposes dropping its partitions. Never answer yes to a prompt that drops `gl_entries_p*`.\n- Do not touch the development database or the running development server unless asked. Do not drop tables or decrypt stored credentials without an explicit instruction.\n- Stop servers with `fuser -k <port>/tcp`, never `pkill -f` with a pattern that appears in your own command line.\n\nContents of /home/paullaster/.claude/projects/-home-paullaster-Documents-projects-bigbro-qsell/memory/MEMORY.md (user's auto-memory, persists across conversations):\n\n- [Responsive & accessible UI](responsive-accessible-ui.md) — standing rule: all qsell UI work must be responsive + accessible, high-traffic code standards\n- [Verification setup](qsell-verification-setup.md) — isolated e2e on :3100 + throwaway DB; ESLint crash workaround\n- [KRA TIMS/eTIMS design](kra-tims-etims-design.md) — separate code columns, strict hard-fail mode resolution, eTIMS-only transmission\n- [Reports module](reports-module.md) — Business Overview foundation: per-section permissions, data sources, definitions, deferred items\n- [Sales order platform](sales-order-platform.md) — blueprint + pricing docs, decisions taken, kernel slices built (decision log, number series), next steps\n- [Core finance design](core-finance-design.md) — GL/CoA/journals/receivables/wallet/refund/M-Pesa; doc approved, F-0, F-1 and F-1c built; decisions, deviations, lessons\n- [Project non-negotiables](project-non-negotiables.md) — permanent rules: quality bar + tamper-resistant security, server components with zero logic in components, never trust client data, enterprise Autocomplete (never select), non-blocking parallel loading, full test pyramid, ESLint 10.12+\n- [Next.js parallel/intercepting routes](nextjs-parallel-and-intercepting-routes.md) — Next 16.3.4 docs digest: slots, default.tsx, (.) interception, Suspense/use() parallel loading, qsell's @modal/@create setup\n- [Next.js 16.4.0 default](nextjs-16-4-default-version.md) — default version + folder-structure rule; 16.4 features (Cache Components, ensureStatic, navigation()/prefetch()); repo still on 16.3.4; upgrade checklist\n- [Pinned stack versions](pinned-stack-versions.md) — non-negotiable Next 16.4.0, React 19.3.0, ESLint 10.12.0, TS ~7.0.2; TS 7 rules; known conflicts (typescript-eslint peer, baseUrl, eslint-config-next, @types)\n- [Quotes/templates/Autocomplete status](quotes-templates-autocomplete-status.md) — what is built (Autocomplete, lookups, server-side swaps, intercepted routes) and what remains against the rules\n- [Finance rules compliance](finance-rules-compliance.md) — what of finance/payments was brought up to the non-negotiables (Payments screens done) and the remaining debt in order\n- [No attribution in commits](no-attribution-in-commits.md) — permanent: never add Co-Authored-By / \"Generated with\" lines to commits or PRs\n</system-reminder>"},{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>\nAs you answer the user's questions, you can use the following context:\n# userEmail\nThe user's email address is paullasterokoth98@gmail.com. The GitHub Environment is correct**\n```sh\ngh variable list --env noels-deliveries\ngh secret list --env noels-deliveries\n```\n`PUBLIC_DOMAIN` should be `shop.noelsdeliveries.com`. The three secrets should be listed. Neither command prints secret values.\n\n**Run the deploy**\n1. Go to Actions → **Deploy release to instance** → Run workflow.\n2. Use branch `release`, Environment ID `noels-deliveries`, and leave the SHA empty. It then picks the newest successful `release` build.\n3. Watch the run. The order is: validate → pull → migrate → start → health check → write the Nginx snippet.\n\nThe last step may warn that Nginx doesn't include `noels-deliveries.conf` yet. That's expected, and phase H fixes it.\n\n**Check the result on the server**\n```sh\ncd /opt/qsell/instances/noels-deliveries\ndocker compose --env-file .env.deploy -f compose.production.yaml ps\ncurl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/health\nls deploy/nginx/\n```\nYou should see `db`, `app`, `worker` and `caddy` running and healthy, and `noels-deliveries.conf` in `deploy/nginx/`. If the compose command complains about file names, run `ls -a` in that directory and send me the output.\n\n**If it fails**\nPaste the failing step's log. The likely causes are a bad GHCR token or a host key mismatch (both come from phase F), or a missing image because the build hasn't finished.
